Renesas is hiring a Product Assurance Manager to help lead quality execution for its rapidly growing Module business within the Performance Core Power group. This role is being created to address the increasing complexity of our module manufacturing footprint, and will serve as the primary connective tissue between our customers, our external manufacturing partners, and our internal teams to ensure that every module we ship meets the quality bar our customers expect, on time.  You will own the customer-facing negotiation of quality and manufacturing specifications, translating customer requirements into clear, actionable standards that can be executed across our manufacturing flows. You will then work directly with our external manufacturing partners and ODMs to assess, qualify, and continuously monitor their quality systems and processes, ensuring they are capable of meeting the specifications agreed upon with our customers.  When quality issues arise, you will act as the quarterback for resolution — driving root-cause analysis, pulling in cross-functional teams (design, test, product, applications, manufacturing, supply chain, and customer-facing teams) as needed, and ensuring corrective and preventive actions are implemented quickly and effectively. This is a highly cross-functional, externally facing role for someone who is comfortable owning outcomes without owning every function involved in delivering them.  Success in this role will be measured by on-time, quality delivery of products to customers, speed and effectiveness of quality issue resolution, and the strength and reliability of our external manufacturing partners' quality systems.   Key Responsibilities:    Serve as the primary point of contact with external customers to negotiate and finalize quality and manufacturing specifications for module products.  Partner with external manufacturing partners and ODMs to evaluate, qualify, and continuously monitor their quality processes and standards against agreed customer specifications.  Act as the quarterback for quality issue resolution — leading root-cause analysis and pulling in cross-functional teams (engineering, manufacturing, test, supply chain, and customer teams) as needed to drive rapid containment and closure.  Own on-time, quality delivery of finished products to customers, proactively identifying and escalating risks before they impact schedule or quality.  Translate customer-specific quality requirements into clear specifications and drive their adoption across manufacturing partners and internal teams.  Track and report quality metrics and open issues to internal leadership and customer QA teams, ensuring alignment and transparency on status.  Drive corrective and preventive action (CAPA) plans to closure with external partners, verifying effectiveness before issues are considered resolved.  Support structured problem-solving methodologies (e.g., 8D, DMAIC) across partners and internal teams to build durable, repeatable quality processes.  Build strong working relationships with customer quality organizations and external manufacturing partners to enable fast, collaborative resolution of issues.     10+ years of experience in any one of a broad set of roles including quality engineering, product assurance, or manufacturing in the factory.  Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, materials science, or a related technical field.  Strong communication and relationship-management skills, with demonstrated ability to negotiate specifications directly with customers.  Experience working with external manufacturing partners, contract manufacturers, or ODMs on quality processes and standards.  Working knowledge of root-cause analysis and structured problem-solving methodologies (e.g., 8D, 5-Why, DMAIC).  Ability to lead cross-functional teams through complex, time-sensitive quality issues without direct authority over all functions involved.  Comfort operating in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment as part of a newly created role supporting a growing product line.  Strong experience with semiconductor or module manufacturing flows, especially SMT, and supply chain dynamics is required. This role is responsible for  leading OSAT  strategic engagement and commercial management, driving cost optimization, ensuring supply continuity, and owning end-to-end supplier strategy. The role requires strong leadership, program management, and cross-functional influence to align business, engineering, and supply chain objectives while driving long-term value creation.   Key Responsibilities     Lead  commercial negotiations including pricing, LTAs, capacity agreements, price adjustments, and payment terms.   Own  OSAT supplier strategy and act as a key decision driver in supplier selection.   Drive  cost optimization initiatives using structured methodologies such as cost breakdown analysis, should-cost modeling, VA/VE, and localization strategies.   Lead cross-functional  program engagement as a product/program management partner, ensuring OSAT readiness across MP, NPI, transfer, ramp-up, and EOL phases.   Ensure  supply continuity and resilience by proactively managing capacity planning, allocation strategies, and supply risk mitigation.   Identify, assess,  and  mitigate  supply chain risks including capacity constraints, geopolitical exposure, cost volatility, and supplier dependency.   Lead  contract governance including MSA, NDA, pricing frameworks, and commercial agreements, ensuring alignment with business strategy.   Drive  supplier performance management through structured reviews, KPI tracking, and continuous improvement initiatives.   Lead  escalation management and resolution of critical issues related to quality, delivery, capacity, and commercial disputes, working with stakeholders internally and externally.   Act  as a strategic interface between internal functions (Engineering, Product Group, Supply Chain, and Finance teams) and OSAT partners to ensure alignment of roadmap, cost, and execution priorities.     3+ years of purchasing/procurement experience, preferably in the semiconductor or electronics industry.  Fluent in English is required; Japanese language proficiency is a plus.   Hands-on experience or familiarity with power-related products and components is a strong advantage.   Advanced Excel and data analysis skills; proficient in PowerPoint for executive-level presentations.  Strong stakeholder management, communication, and negotiation skills with the ability to influence cross-functional teams and senior stakeholders.  Experience in strategic sourcing, supplier management, or program management is highly preferred. We are looking for a highly technical Senior Analytics Engineer to own and evolve our end-to-end product analytics platform.  This role is responsible for the complete analytics data lifecycle — starting with analytics instrumentation embedded in product source code, through event collection and ingestion, raw data storage, transformation and aggregation pipelines, and ultimately the presentation of trusted analytics through dashboards, reports, and analytical tools.  The successful candidate will act as the owner of the analytics flow, ensuring that analytics data is accurate, reliable, scalable, well-defined, and usable across the organization.  This is not primarily a dashboard-building or reporting role. It is an engineering-focused position responsible for the architecture, implementation, operation, and continuous improvement of the analytics platform.  Key Responsibilities   End-to-End Analytics Platform Ownership  Product Analytics Instrumentation  Data Collection and Raw Data Layer  Data Pipelines, Importers, and Processing  Analytics Data Models and Metrics  Analytics Presentation Layer  Data Quality and Observability  Analytics Governance   Expected Outcomes  The successful candidate will establish a clear and reliable analytics platform where:   Product teams have a standardized way to instrument new functionality.  Analytics events are consistently defined and documented.  Data reliably reaches the analytics platform from production systems.  Raw data remains available for investigation and reprocessing.  Transformations and aggregations are automated and maintainable.  Important metrics have clear and consistent definitions.  Data quality issues are detected proactively rather than discovered through incorrect dashboards.  Business and product teams can confidently use analytics tools for decision-making.  Every important metric can be traced back to its underlying product events and data sources.  The analytics platform has clear technical ownership.        Strong software engineering and data engineering background.  Hands-on experience building and operating production analytics or data platforms.  Advanced SQL skills.  Experience designing ETL/ELT and data transformation pipelines.  Experience with event-based product analytics.  Understanding of analytics instrumentation within web applications, backend services, and distributed systems.  Experience working with data lakes, data warehouses, or lakehouse architectures.  Experience designing analytical data models and aggregation pipelines.  Experience with BI and analytics visualization platforms.  Strong understanding of data quality, lineage, observability, and governance.  Ability to troubleshoot data issues across multiple layers — from application source code to the final dashboard.  Ability to work directly with software engineers and review or contribute to analytics-related application code. We are looking for an experienced and visionary Functional Safety Architect to define, drive, and govern functional safety concepts for next-generation industrial systems. In this role, you will lead system-level safety architecture across hardware, software, and system boundaries, ensuring compliance with international functional safety standards for industrial, automation, robotics, and energy applications.  You will act as the technical authority for functional safety, bridging customer safety requirements, market regulations, and product engineering. Your work will ensure that our industrial solutions achieve the highest levels of safety, reliability, and regulatory compliance while enabling innovation and time-to-market.  Key Responsibilities   Define and own the system-level functional safety architecture for industrial applications, covering sensors, MCUs/SoCs, power devices, actuators, and communication interfaces.  Translate safety requirements from standards, regulations, and customer use cases into system, hardware, and software safety requirements.  Lead hazard analysis and risk assessment activities (HARA), safety concept development, and safety lifecycle planning.  Define safety mechanisms, diagnostics, redundancy concepts, and fault-handling strategies across HW/SW boundaries.  Ensure alignment with functional safety standards such as IEC 61508, IEC 62061, ISO 13849, and related sector-specific standards.  Drive HW/SW partitioning decisions with a focus on safety integrity, freedom from interference, and fault containment.  Specify and review safety requirements, Safety Requirements Specifications (SRS), safety manuals, and safety case documentation.  Collaborate closely with Product Groups, system architects, hardware, software, and validation teams to ensure end-to-end safety integrity.  Support product definition and roadmaps by assessing safety implications, certification effort, and architectural trade-offs.  Guide and review safety-related design, implementation, verification, and validation activities across the product lifecycle.  Interface with customers, assessors, and certification bodies to support safety assessments, audits, and certifications.  Support customer engagements by explaining safety concepts, assumptions of use, and integration guidelines.  Monitor industry trends, evolving standards, and regulatory requirements, and integrate insights into safety strategies and architectures.  Contribute to reference architectures, application notes, and safety concept reuse across multiple industrial platforms.  Provide functional safety training, mentoring, and technical guidance to internal engineering and application teams.     Master’s or Ph.D. degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechatronics, Systems Engineering, or a related field.  8+ years of experience in embedded or industrial system development, with significant responsibility in functional safety.  Proven track record as a Functional Safety Architect, Safety Manager, or Lead Safety Engineer for industrial or automation systems.  Deep understanding of functional safety standards such as IEC 61508, IEC 62061, ISO 13849, and their application to industrial equipment.  Strong experience with safety lifecycle activities including HARA, safety concept definition, safety analysis (FMEA, FMEDA, FTA), and safety validation.  Solid knowledge of embedded systems architecture, microcontrollers/SoCs, real-time software, and industrial communication protocols (e.g., CAN, EtherCAT, PROFINET, Modbus).  Experience defining and assessing safety mechanisms such as diagnostics, watchdogs, redundancy, diversity, and safe-state concepts.  Ability to work cross-functionally and communicate complex safety topics clearly to engineering, business, customers, and assessors.  Strong documentation skills and experience preparing safety-related documentation for internal and external stakeholders.    Nice to Have   • Functional Safety certification (e.g., TÜV Functional Safety Engineer/Professional). 
• Experience with cybersecurity and its interaction with functional safety in industrial systems. 
• Background in robotics, motion control, motor drives, or industrial power conversion. 
• Familiarity with semiconductor safety architectures, safety libraries, and safety-certified IP. 
• Experience supporting third-party assessments and certifications with notified bodies.     Renesas is an embedded semiconductor solution provider driven by its Purpose,  To Make Our Lives Easier . 【 募集背景】  
エッジAIデバイスから工場設備、データセンター用途まで、産業用プロセッサの適用領域は急速に拡大しています。こうした中、製造業や医療分野などでは、組込み機器を含むシステムのサイバーセキュリティ対策が社会的な課題となっています。そのため、産業向け組込み製品には高度な機能性と高いセキュリティレベルの両立が求められており、オープンソースソフトウェアを活用した機能拡充や、最新のセキュリティ技術を製品へ適用することが重要なテーマとなっています。 
本ポジションでは、デバイスドライバの開発や既存ソフトウェアのポーティングにとどまらず、新しい産業規格や先端的なセキュリティ技術への対応を、グローバルな開発体制のもとで、オープンソースコミュニティと連携しながら推進していただきます。 
Linuxを中心としたオープンソース技術や組込み機器向けセキュリティ技術の開発に実践的に取り組み、その成果を実製品として世に送り出す経験ができます。 
これらの分野に関心を持ち、製品化に意欲を持って取り組みたいエンジニアを募集します。   【主な業務内容】  
Renesas RZ MPU向けに、LSI設計部門や国内外のOSSコミュニティ等と連携しながら、Linux関連ソフトウェアの設計・開発を担うポジションです。

【Backgroud】   The application scope of industrial processors is rapidly expanding, ranging from edge AI devices to factory equipment and data center applications. In this context, ensuring cybersecurity for systems that include embedded devices has become a significant societal challenge in sectors such as manufacturing and healthcare.  As a result, embedded products for industrial use are required to achieve both advanced functionality and a high level of security. Expanding product capabilities through the use of open source software and applying the latest security technologies to products have become key priorities.  In this position, you will be responsible not only for device driver development and porting of existing software, but also for addressing emerging industrial standards and advanced security technologies. You will drive these initiatives as part of a global development team, working in collaboration with open source communities.  You will gain hands-on experience in developing open source technologies, particularly Linux-based platforms, as well as security technologies for embedded systems, and delivering these innovations as products to the market.  We are looking for engineers who have a strong interest in these areas and are motivated to contribute to bringing products to market.   【Job Description】   This position is responsible for the design and development of Linux-related software for our industrial high-end processor, RZ series, in collaboration with internal LSI design teams and both domestic and international open source communities. Why Altium?   Build the web platform that presents Altium to the world. Our web team owns Altium's public web properties — the main marketing site, documentation portal, customer dashboard, resource centre and localized regional sites — serving high traffic across roughly ten locales. These are some of the contributions you might make to Altium's web platform:    Building headless Next.js / React applications consuming Drupal data over GraphQL    Driving the migration from a Drupal-themed frontend to a modern Next.js stack    Building and maintaining a shared design system on Radix UI, shadcn/ui and Tailwind CSS    Owning the rendering, caching and data-fetching decisions that sit between frontend and CMS    Altium offers the opportunity to shape the frontend architecture of a high-traffic, multi-locale web platform and to move it forward while it keeps running in production    About the Role   Your primary role will be building and evolving the frontend of Altium's web properties, primarily as headless Next.js applications consuming data from Drupal over GraphQL, while keeping the existing Drupal-integrated frontend stable and visually consistent during the ongoing migration. We are hiring for depth in React, Next.js and TypeScript — not for prior Drupal knowledge. Our Drupal frontend layer and deployment specifics are things a strong frontend engineer picks up in a few weeks, and we will support that ramp-up.   A Day in the Life of Our Senior Frontend Developer     Develop features and components in Next.js, React and TypeScript, using the App Router and React Server Components and choosing the right rendering strategy per page    Integrate applications with Drupal via GraphQL and Apollo Client; implement content freshness with ISR and on-demand revalidation    Build and maintain reusable UI components on Radix UI, shadcn/ui and Tailwind CSS, aligned with the design system    Maintain and extend existing Drupal themes (Twig templates, SCSS, Pug-based markup build, Webpack)    Own Core Web Vitals, accessibility and technical SEO for the pages you ship    Write component tests, contribute to the shared Playwright E2E suite and investigate production incidents with Sentry    Participate in code review and contribute to engineering standards and codebase health      Who We're Looking For     4+ years of commercial React experience, including at least 2 years with Next.js in production    Owns a feature end to end — from design handoff through rollout and post-release verification    Traces a production incident from an error report to root cause without hand-holding    Makes technical decisions, states trade-offs explicitly, and updates a position when evidence changes it    Treats visual regressions, accessibility and performance as part of "done", not as follow-up work    Pragmatic about legacy: willing to maintain an existing Drupal-integrated frontend while helping move the platform forward    Reviews others' code constructively and raises the standard of the codebase around them     
 Required Technology Experience     Strong JavaScript and TypeScript (strict mode)    Next.js App Router and React Server Components in production    Client-side GraphQL (Apollo Client or equivalent)    Tailwind CSS; component library and design system principles    Frontend caching: ISR, on-demand revalidation, TTLs and cache invalidation    Core Web Vitals and the tooling to measure and diagnose them    Web accessibility standards    Multi-locale applications    SCSS and at least one template engine (Pug, Twig or similar); Webpack and frontend build pipelines    Git and code review     
 Nice to Have     Drupal theming: templates, theme libraries, integrating markup    Storybook or another component workshop    Image and performance optimization with Next Image and Sharp    Redis and cache strategy / invalidation design    Marketing site instrumentation: GTM, dataLayer, consent management (e.g. OneTrust)    Technical SEO depth: structured data, sitemaps, hreflang across locales

Design and simulate power stage circuits (e.g., synchronous buck/boost, multiphase, half-bridge/DrMOS, gate drivers) used to validate device performance under realistic switching and thermal conditions.  Select and characterize power devices (LDMOS, trench MOSFETs, LV GaN HEMTs, Schottky/sync rectifiers) for inclusion in test structures, working with device/process engineering on layout-dependent tradeoffs (RDS(ON), Qg, breakdown voltage, SOA).  Perform IC-level layout and design for test structures, including parasitic-aware layout for switch nodes, current sensing, and gate drive paths.  Extend designs to module/package level as needed — co-design of power stages with packaging, magnetics, and PCB layout for evaluation boards and system-level test vehicles.  Develop test and characterization plans covering DC parametrics, switching performance, efficiency, transient response, and voltage/current stress margins (including switch-node ringing and abs-max validation).  Lead or support silicon bring-up, debug, and correlation of measured results against simulation and design targets.  Collaborate cross-functionally with process integration, reliability, product/applications engineering, and test engineering to close the loop from process split data to product-ready specifications.  Document design methodology, test vehicle results, and characterization data to support technology qualification and product development decisions.     Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Microelectronics, or related field.  10+ years of hands-on design experience in power semiconductor devices, analog/power ICs, or power electronics.  Strong working knowledge of power conversion topologies (e.g., buck, boost, multiphase/interleaved converters, half-bridge, DrMOS/Intelli-Phase-style architectures) and how topology choices drive device requirements.  Solid understanding of power device physics and tradeoffs across BCD process technologies and GaN (particularly low-voltage GaN HEMTs) — including RDS(ON), switching loss, gate charge, breakdown/avalanche behavior, and thermal characteristics.  Demonstrated experience designing test structures or test chips/vehicles for process technology development (not just product design) — comfortable defining what a process node needs to prove out.  IC-level design and layout experience, including parasitic-sensitive layout practices for high-current switching nodes.  Experience taking designs beyond the die level to module, package, or board level (e.g., power module co-design, evaluation board layout, thermal/electrical co-design).  Proficiency with circuit simulation tools (SPICE or equivalent) and familiarity with device/TCAD simulation concepts.  Ability to interpret and specify absolute maximum ratings, transient voltage tolerance, and protection thresholds (OVP/UVP/OCP/OTP) relevant to power stage reliability.  Strong lab skills: bring-up, debug, and characterization using oscilloscopes, curve tracers, power analyzers, and thermal imaging.    The expected annual pay range for this position is $180K - $230K. Strong communication, presentation, and documentation skills with the ability to work effectively in a team environment. We are seeking a highly capable Senior Field Applications Engineer (FAE) to support strategic customers across datacenter, AI, server, and advanced computing markets. This role is based in the San Jose, CA area.  This position combines strong hands on technical execution, customer facing support, and system level power expertise. The ideal candidate brings experience in power electronics and board level debug, with the ability to support customers through design, bring up, validation, and issue resolution. This role is well suited for an experienced engineer who can work independently on complex technical issues while collaborating effectively across internal and customer teams.  Renesas provides comprehensive training on our digital multiphase power solutions, helping new engineers build expertise in our architectures, tools, and validation methodologies.  Responsibilities   1. Customer Facing Technical Support   · Serve as a key technical interface for customer accounts, supporting power architecture and voltage regulator engagements from design phase through production.  · Provide technical guidance on digital multiphase power controllers, power modules, and server class power delivery solutions.  · Support schematic reviews, layout reviews, board bring up, debug, and validation activities.  · Generate customer facing technical materials including program updates, validation reports, controller configuration files, issue summaries, and supporting waveform data.  · Assist customers during system validation, including VR performance, telemetry, protection behavior, and interaction with CPU, GPU, ASIC, or SoC power domains.   2. VR Simulation and Validation   · Perform VR solution simulations with application specific PDNs in SIMPLIS to support design reviews and early risk reduction.  · Execute validation of multiphase power solutions for datacenter and AI platforms, including transient response, efficiency, telemetry, fault behavior, and protection features.  · Develop and maintain test plans, validation checklists, and coverage matrices to ensure thorough evaluation across operating conditions.  · Use lab instrumentation and structured test methods to support repeatable, high quality validation.   3. Debug and Root Cause Analysis   · Diagnose complex electrical and system issues using oscilloscopes, electronic loads, current probes, network analyzers, power supplies, and related lab equipment.  · Drive issue resolution with urgency, including support for high priority customer escalations.  · Partner with design, systems, and applications teams to identify root cause and help define corrective actions.  · Escalate appropriately when deeper cross functional support is needed, while maintaining ownership of customer communication and follow through.   4. Program Execution and Technical Ownership   · Work closely with Sales, Product Line, Marketing, and engineering teams to support successful customer engagements and design wins.  · Manage multiple customer activities in parallel, including design support, validation efforts, debug tasks, and issue tracking.  · Drive execution against customer milestones and internal priorities with strong attention to detail and responsiveness.  · Help mitigate technical risk on active programs by identifying issues early and driving timely action.  · Support successful design adoption by combining technical depth with practical judgment on where to focus effort for highest customer and business impact.   ·   Required    · BS or MS in Electrical Engineering or related field.  · 5+ years of experience in power electronics, voltage regulator validation, power applications, or system level power architecture.  · Strong hands on experience with bench level electrical testing and debug methodologies.  · Working knowledge of oscilloscopes, function generators, electronic loads, power supplies, current probes, and soldering tools.  · Experience supporting customer technical issues through structured debug and problem solving.  · Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with both engineers and customer stakeholders.  · Ability to manage multiple concurrent technical activities with a strong sense of urgency and ownership.   Preferred   · Experience supporting AI, ML, CPU, GPU, or server power delivery applications.  · Hands on experience with:   multiphase buck converters and digital VR controllers  high current server or AI power designs  SIMPLIS simulation environment   · Familiarity with validation planning, test automation, and lab instrumentation workflows.  · Experience working directly with strategic customers in a field applications, systems, or product applications role.  · Ability to balance technical problem solving with commercial awareness in support of design win execution.          What Success Looks Like in This Role   · Builds credibility quickly with customers through strong technical execution and consultative engagement.  · Supports successful design progress and helps reduce technical risk on active programs.  · Handles multiple customer priorities effectively, including urgent escalations.  · Contributes positively to team execution, customer satisfaction, and business results.     The expected annual pay range for this position is $120-$168K. The Staff Power Architect – System Design is responsible for architecture definition, modeling, and technical leadership for PMIC and advanced DC/DC converter products. This role provides architectural ownership and technical leadership from concept through silicon validation. The role works closely with analog design, digital, verification, validation, test, and product engineering teams to ensure alignment of architecture intent, implementation, and verification across multiple programs.   Key Responsibilities   System Architecture & Technical Leadership  - Define and own architectures for PMIC and advanced power converter products across multiple programs.  - Drive architecture trade-offs and define operating modes, startup and shutdown sequencing, and system boundary conditions.  - Lead architecture reviews and remain deeply involved during the design phase to ensure the transition from architecture to design execution is carried out correctly.  - Provide architectural leadership and technical guidance for system-level design decisions across projects.   Modeling & Analysis   - Develop and maintain low-level and system-level models to support architecture decisions and risk reduction, using tools such as Simplis.  - Analyze stability, transient response, fault behavior, and corner cases to support architecture definition and validation.  - Provide model-based insight to support analog design convergence and reduce silicon risk.   Cross-Functional Collaboration   - Collaborate with analog design, digital, verification, validation, test, and applications teams to ensure architecture intent is implemented and verified.  - Participate in design and architecture reviews and technical discussions across multiple programs.  - Provide technical guidance during silicon validation and system-level debug activities.   Documentation & Knowledge Capture   - Create and maintain architecture documentation, design guidelines, and best-practice references.  - Create detailed sub-block specifications that enable design and verification teams to execute implementation and verification activities efficiently.  - Capture lessons learned, root causes, and preventive actions to improve future designs.  - Contribute to internal training, workshops, and technical knowledge-sharing activities.       Required Qualifications   - Strong experience in PMICs, DC/DC converters, or mixed-signal power systems.  - Experience with architecture definition and architectural analysis for power management products.  - Familiarity with modeling tools such as Simplis and Simulink.  - Ability to work across disciplines and influence technical decisions through collaboration and technical credibility.  - Strong written and verbal communication skills for technical documentation and reviews.   Nice to Have   - Experience contributing to advanced power converter programs.  - Familiarity with emerging architectures such as Multi-Level Converter (MLC) topologies.  - Familiarity with multi-rail power systems and power sequencing.  - Experience supporting silicon bring-up, validation, and root-cause analysis.   What Success Looks Like  - Architectures are clearly defined and consistently implemented across projects. As the Senior Principal Platform Architect for UALink Switch Products, you will be the ultimate system-level authority responsible for defining the end-to-end hardware, software, and management architecture of our next-generation AI scale-up network chassis.   In this role, you will look beyond the individual switch silicon to architect the entire platform ecosystem. You will define how multiple UALink switch ASICs interact across backplanes, determine how the system handles multi-kilowatt power delivery and liquid/air cooling orchestration, and architect the platform management stack (BMC/OpenBMC) that allows the switch to seamlessly integrate into massive hyper-scale data centers. You will bridge the gap between silicon engineering, system hardware design, and cloud software orchestration.   1. System & Topology Architecture     Chassis & Rack Definition: Lead the structural, electrical, and logical design of the UALink switch chassis, defining high-speed backplane topologies, cabled scale-up fabrics, and multi-tier switch hierarchies.       Signal & Power Integrity Collaboration: Partner with electrical and SI/PI engineering teams to define parameters for ultra-high-speed SerDes routing across PCBs, flyover cables, and optical components, minimizing bit error rates (BER).       Scale-Up Fabric Optimization: Architect rack-level and row-level topologies that optimize collective communication paths (e.g., All-Reduce, All-to-All) for tens of thousands of interconnected GPUs.     2. Platform Management & Software Infrastructure     Control Plane & BMC Architecture: Architect the end-to-end system management plane. Define how Baseboard Management Controllers (BMCs) monitor, configure, and provision the switch using OpenBMC, Redfish, and PLDM over MCTP.       Boot & Initialization Flows: Establish platform-level boot sequencing, multi-rail power sequencing, and secure multi-node firmware update orchestration.       Platform Security Architecture: Define the hardware security lifecycle, including Platform Firmware Resiliency (NIST SP 800-193), secure enclave integration, and Component Attestation (SPDM).     3. Advanced RAS & Infrastructure Integration     Platform-Level RAS: Architect system-level Reliability, Availability, and Serviceability (RAS) strategies. Define how the platform isolates hardware faults, routes around failed links, handles hot-swapping of fans, power supplies, and switch blades without dropping the AI training cluster.       Thermal & Power Orchestration: Establish dynamic power management and telemetry frameworks to balance the massive transient power draws of next-generation AI workloads against rack-level cooling limits.      Education & Experience     Degree: Master’s or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.       Experience: 20+ years of architectural experience in high-performance server platforms, hyper-scale network switches, or data center infrastructure.     Technical Skill Set     System-Level Interconnects: Expert knowledge of high-speed platform fabrics and standards (UALink, NVLink, OAM/UBB, PCIe Gen6/Gen7, CXL, or Ultra Ethernet).       Platform Management Standards: Deep expertise in industry-standard management architectures, including Redfish, IPMI, MCTP, SPDM, and OpenBMC.       Hardware-Software Interface: Thorough understanding of OS/VMM kernels, device drivers, and platform initialization frameworks (UEFI, ACPI).       Data Center Infrastructure: Comprehensive grasp of modern rack architectures (e.g., OCP ORv3), liquid cooling management, and high-density 48V/54V power delivery.     Preferred Attributes (Ways to Stand Out)     Proven track record of delivering a high-volume, multi-million-gate switching or compute platform successfully into top-tier hyper-scale cloud providers (AWS, Azure, GCP, Meta).       Active committee leadership or direct specification contributions within the UALink Consortium, Ultra Ethernet Consortium (UEC), or Open Compute Project (OCP).       Experience architecting systems designed for ultra-high-density accelerator form factors (such as Nvidia Blackwell/Vera Rubin grids or AMD Instinct platforms).      The expected annual pay range for this position is $253,000-315,000K. This position is also eligible for bonus opportunities. Please note that final offer amount will be dependent on geographic location, applicable experience, and skillset of the candidate. About the Role & The Reality AI Lab   The Renesas AIoT Center of Excellence in Columbia, MD (formerly Reality AI) is seeking a hands-on Senior Edge AI Applications Engineer to lead our physical lab setup, fabricate sensor prototyping rigs, and deploy low-power machine learning models directly onto microcontrollers (MCUs).  This is a physical, hardware-centric engineering role. You will work at the exact intersection of physical system fabrication, digital signal processing (DSP), C/C++ embedded firmware, and TinyML. You will physically instrument motor control setups, audio arrays, and vibration sensors, collect high-frequency time-series datasets off real physical targets, write DSP feature extraction, and compress ML models to run within kilobytes of RAM on Renesas MCUs.   What This Role IS NOT (Please Read Before Applying)      This IS NOT a Cloud AI, NLP, or LLM Role:  If your primary experience is with LangChain, PySpark, RAG pipelines, or fine-tuning Large Language Models in the cloud, this role is not a fit.     This IS NOT a Remote Software Position:  You will be physically building rigs, soldering, testing hardware with oscilloscopes, and working in our dedicated Columbia, MD lab 100% onsite.     Key Responsibilities      Physical Prototyping & Lab Management:  Hands-on fabrication of physical prototype rigs, custom sensor arrays, and 3D-printed enclosures to capture real-world physical phenomena.     High-Frequency Sensor Data Acquisition:  Instrument physical setups (motors, HVAC, industrial machines, automotive targets) to capture, clean, and preprocess high-frequency time-series datasets (accelerometers, acoustic, electrical, current/voltage).     TinyML & On-Device Model Deployment:  Train, quantize (INT8/FP16), and deploy tiny machine learning models onto microcontrollers (ARM Cortex-M, Renesas RA/RX/RL78) using TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers, CMSIS-NN, or eIQ.     Digital Signal Processing (DSP):  Apply DSP feature extraction (FFT, spectrograms, windowing, bandpass filtering, time-domain features) to feed edge inference pipelines.     Embedded Firmware & Driver Development:  Write C/C++ code, bare-metal or RTOS drivers (FreeRTOS, Zephyr), and handle low-level communication (SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, DMA).     Technical Leadership:  Lead junior lab engineers, manage physical lab setups, and collaborate cross-functionally with product and systems teams.       Education:  B.S., M.S., or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Applied Physics, or a related technical field.    Experience:  3+ years of hands-on experience in embedded systems, hardware prototyping, and deploying edge ML/DSP algorithms onto physical hardware targets.     Hardware & Prototyping Skills:  Proven experience with physical assembly, breadboarding, soldering, 3D printing, schematic reading, and bench debugging using JTAG/SWD, oscilloscopes, and logic analyzers.     Signal Processing (DSP):  Demonstrated fluency in time-series and audio signal processing (spectral analysis, filtering, feature extraction in Python/MATLAB).     Firmware & Embedded C/C++:  Hands-on C/C++ programming for MCUs, RTOS task management, DMA queues, and low-level peripheral drivers.     On-Device ML:  Practical experience with TinyML frameworks (TensorFlow Lite Micro, CMSIS-NN, Edge Impulse) and model quantization/compression for constrained MCU targets. About the Role & The Reality AI Lab   The Renesas AIoT Center of Excellence in Columbia, MD (formerly Reality AI) is seeking a hands-on Senior Edge AI Applications Engineer to build and deploy edge AI solutions that integrate machine learning with real-world hardware systems.  In this role, you will work directly in our physical lab facility, executing proof-of-concept (PoC) hardware builds, assembling custom sensor setups, and deploying low-power ML models onto microcontrollers. You will operate at the exact intersection of small-scale physical fabrication, digital signal processing (DSP), C/C++ embedded firmware, and microcontroller-level TinyML deployment.  You will execute non-visual sensing solutions - instrumenting physical hardware setups (industrial motors, automotive systems, consumer devices), collecting high-frequency time-series sensor data, building custom DSP pipelines, and optimizing tiny machine learning models to run on Renesas silicon.  Are you an Embedded Engineer or Applied Physicist who thrives in a physical lab environment building custom sensor rigs, soldering prototype boards, and squeezing machine learning models onto microcontrollers?   ATTENTION APPLICANTS: READ BEFORE APPLYING     This is a physical lab execution and embedded hardware role.     DO NOT APPLY  if your background is strictly in Cloud AI, Data Science, Generative AI, LLMs, LangChain, or Web Backend APIs.     DO APPLY  if you have 2–3+ years of experience building physical prototype rigs, writing embedded C/C++, running FFTs on raw accelerometer/acoustic data, debugging SPI/I2C signals with an oscilloscope, and running TinyML on bare-metal silicon.     Key Responsibilities      Physical Prototyping & Fabrication:  Hands-on assembly of prototype rigs, sensor arrays, 3D-printed mounts, and microelectronic setups to capture real-world physical data.     High-Frequency Sensor Data Engineering:  Instrument physical systems to capture, clean, and preprocess high-frequency time-series datasets (acoustic, vibration, electrical, motor current).     DSP & TinyML Deployment:  Build DSP feature extraction pipelines (FFTs, spectral analysis, filtering) and deploy optimized, quantized TinyML models onto microcontrollers (ARM Cortex-M, Renesas RA/RX/RL78) using TFLite Micro, CMSIS-NN, or eIQ.     Embedded Firmware Development:  Write real-time C/C++ firmware, bare-metal or RTOS drivers (FreeRTOS, Zephyr), DMA buffer management, and low-level peripheral communication (SPI, I2C, UART, CAN).     Customer & Cross-BU Collaboration:  Work directly with customers and internal product teams to ingest raw hardware telemetry, debug edge firmware issues, and demonstrate working hardware solutions.     Technical Leadership & Mentorship:  Lead junior engineers on lab tasks, document engineering best practices, and contribute technical leadership across cross-functional teams.     Why Join Renesas?      No SCIF / No Clearance:  Enjoy complex signal processing and hardware challenges without defense contractor bureaucracy or classified workspace restrictions.     Commercial Product Impact:  What you build in our lab gets integrated into Renesas silicon and deployed into millions of industrial, automotive, and consumer devices globally.     Startup Autonomy + Global Backing:  Small-team environment (under 50 people in Columbia) backed by one of the world's premier semiconductor manufacturers.       Education:  B.S. or Master’s in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Applied Physics, or a related technical discipline.    Career Experience:  2–3+ years of hands-on career experience in embedded software, physical hardware prototyping, digital signal processing, and real-time edge computing.     Hardware & Lab Skills:  Practical experience in physical system fabrication, 3D printing, electrical assembly, PCB bring-up, and low-level debugging with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and JTAG/SWD.     Embedded Firmware:  Strong C/C++ programming for constrained microcontrollers, bare-metal or RTOS (FreeRTOS, Zephyr), DMA buffer management, and low-level drivers (SPI, I2C, UART, CAN).     Signal Processing & On-Device ML:  Solid understanding of digital signal processing (DSP) for time-series/audio data and practical experience deploying quantized ML models directly onto microcontrollers. Are you a Senior Embedded Engineer or Applied Physicist who thrives in a physical lab environment building custom sensor rigs, soldering prototype boards, and squeezing machine learning models onto microcontrollers?   ATTENTION APPLICANTS: READ BEFORE APPLYING    This is a physical lab leadership and embedded hardware role.    DO NOT APPLY  if your background is strictly in Cloud AI, Data Science, Generative AI, LLMs, LangChain, or Web Backend APIs.     DO APPLY  if you have 7+ years of experience building physical prototype rigs, writing embedded C/C++, running FFTs on raw accelerometer/acoustic data, debugging SPI/I2C signals with an oscilloscope, and running TinyML on bare-metal silicon.     Key Responsibilities      Lab Ownership & Technical Leadership:  Manage physical lab facilities, equipment, part procurement, and project scheduling for customer PoCs, internal R&D, and cross-BU hardware integrations.     Physical Prototyping & Fabrication:  Lead hands-on assembly of prototype rigs, sensor arrays, 3D-printed mounts, and microelectronic setups to capture real-world physical data.     High-Frequency Sensor Data Engineering:  Instrument physical systems to capture, clean, and preprocess high-frequency time-series datasets (acoustic, vibration, electrical, motor current).     DSP & TinyML Deployment:  Design DSP feature extraction pipelines (FFTs, spectral analysis, filtering) and deploy optimized, quantized TinyML models onto microcontrollers (ARM Cortex-M, Renesas RA/RX/RL78) using TFLite Micro, CMSIS-NN, or eIQ.     Customer & Cross-BU Collaboration:  Work directly with customers and internal product teams to ingest raw hardware telemetry, debug edge firmware issues, and demonstrate live hardware solutions.     Team Mentorship:  Lead, mentor, and guide junior lab engineers in firmware debugging, signal processing, and physical prototype fabrication.     Why Join Renesas?      No SCIF / No Clearance:  Enjoy complex signal processing and hardware challenges without defense contractor bureaucracy or classified workspace restrictions.     Commercial Product Impact:  What you build in our lab gets integrated into Renesas silicon and deployed into millions of industrial, automotive, and consumer devices globally.     Startup Autonomy + Global Backing:  Small-team environment (under 50 people in Columbia) backed by one of the world's premier semiconductor manufacturers.       Education:  M.S. or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Applied Physics, or a related technical discipline. (BSEE with extensive, demonstrable lab leadership experience will also be evaluated).    Career Experience:  7–12+ years of hands-on experience in embedded software, physical hardware prototyping, digital signal processing, and real-time edge computing.     Hardware & Lab Skills:  Proven expertise in physical system fabrication, 3D printing, electrical assembly, PCB bring-up, and low-level debugging with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and JTAG/SWD.     Embedded Firmware:  Strong C/C++ programming for constrained microcontrollers, bare-metal or RTOS (FreeRTOS, Zephyr), DMA buffer management, and low-level drivers (SPI, I2C, UART, CAN).     Signal Processing & On-Device ML:  Deep understanding of digital signal processing (DSP) for time-series/audio data and practical experience deploying quantized ML models directly onto microcontrollers. This role is designed for a recent graduate, a master’s graduate, or an early-career professional with hands-on experience gained through coursework, internships, projects, or related work. In this role, you will work with developers and operations leads to implement secure cloud practices, maintain automated deployment pipelines, monitor security posture, document controls, and support the responsible use of AI-assisted engineering tools. This is an opportunity to build practical experience with Infrastructure as Code (IaC), continuous integration, DevSecOps practices, production web operations, cloud security, and secure AI-enabled development workflows.   Responsibilities    AI Infrastructure and Pipeline Security: As we move to adopt a more AI / Agentic workflow you will help secure emerging AI infrastructure and AI-enabled development by supporting security checks, documenting controls, validating tool configurations, and escalating potential risks under guidance from senior team members.  Security Monitoring: Review logs, alerts, system activity, and pipeline outputs to help identify, document, and escalate potential vulnerabilities or unusual behavior.  Cloud Infrastructure Support: Assist in provisioning, configuring, and maintaining core AWS services such as VPC, EC2, S3, IAM, Lambda, Docker, and Kubernetes.  Infrastructure as Code: Learn, update, and write basic Terraform, Serverless, or AWS CloudFormation templates under guidance from senior team members.  Access Management: Help manage user permissions and access controls using AWS IAM and least-privilege principles.  Team Collaboration: Work with developers, QA, and operations team members to troubleshoot issues, document findings, and support safe releases for customer-facing web platforms.  Deployment Support: Help maintain and improve automated CI/CD pipelines to support safe, reliable, and repeatable software delivery.  Documentation: Create and maintain clear technical documentation for architecture diagrams, deployment processes, access controls, and security protocols.     Required Technical Skills    Cloud Fundamentals: Foundational understanding of AWS services, cloud computing concepts, networking basics, IAM, security groups, and common web infrastructure patterns.  Cloud Security Fundamentals: Basic familiarity with least privilege, access controls, encryption, secrets management, logging, and secure configuration practices.  Security Monitoring and Triage: Ability to review logs, alerts, system activity, and pipeline outputs, document findings clearly, and escalate potential risks.  Automation Exposure: Basic experience with scripting languages such as Python or Bash to automate repetitive operational or security-related tasks.  Version Control: Familiarity with Git workflows, Bitbucket pipelines, pull requests, branching strategies, and change tracking.  AI-Assisted Engineering: Awareness of how AI coding assistants and automation tools can be used responsibly, including protecting sensitive information, validating tool outputs, documenting AI-assisted changes, and following approved safe-use practices.    Preferred Qualifications    Experience: 0–2 years of experience in IT support, systems administration, cloud operations, cybersecurity, software engineering, web operations, or a junior DevOps role.  Certifications: Relevant entry-level certifications, such as AWS Cloud Practitioner, CompTIA Security+, or equivalent, are helpful but not required.    Education    Degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Software Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.  Coursework, internships, graduate research, capstone projects, or hands-on work involving cloud security, DevSecOps, secure software development, application security, AI infrastructure, or responsible use of AI coding assistants are highly desirable.    The expected annual base salary range for this position is $65,000 to $85,000. This range does not include potential short-term or long-term incentive compensation. Actual compensation may vary based on relevant experience, skills, qualifications, geographic location, and other job-related factors. 【背景】 
当部門では、今後の製品競争力を左右するCPUアーキテクチャ設計力の強化が急務となっています。 
システムの中核であるCPUは、性能・電力・コスト・安全性のすべてに影響を与えるため、従来以上に高い視点で全体を見渡せるエンジニアが必要です。 
アーキテクチャ検討において最も重要なのは、システム性能を正しく見極める力です。 
単なる理論値や仕様比較ではなく、実際のユースケースやボトルネックを理解し、「どこに性能を割くべきか」「どこを割り切るべきか」を判断できることが求められます。 
そのためには、プログラムを理解し、自ら作れることが不可欠です。 
ソフトウェアの挙動を理解してこそ、CPU構成やメモリ、バス、割り込み設計といったアーキテクチャ上の意思決定が可能になります。 
ハードウェアとソフトウェアの両方を理解した立場から、実効性能に責任を持てるエンジニアを求めています。  【職務概要】 
次世代マイコン／SoC製品に向けたCPUアーキテクチャおよびシステム設計を担当いただきます。 
定量的なKPIに基づくアーキテクチャ策定から、ターゲットアプリケーションを見据えたシステム構築・評価まで、製品競争力の中核を担うポジションです。  【主な業務内容】   CPUアーキテクチャのKPI（性能・電力・面積・拡張性 等）に基づくアーキテクチャ方針の策定  PPA（Performance / Power / Area）ベンチマークの企画・実施および結果分析  ターゲットアプリケーションの要件に沿ったCPU／メモリ／周辺IPを含むシステム構成の設計・構築  アーキテクチャおよびシステム構成におけるトレードオフの整理、技術的根拠に基づく提案  関連部門（ハードウェア設計、ソフトウェア、事業部門 等）との技術的な連携・調整   ※就業場所の変更の範囲、従事すべき業務の変更の範囲については、選考時に詳細をお伝えいたします。       【MUST】    5年以上の実アプリケーション（制御、車載、組込み等）を用いた性能評価・最適化経験  2年以上のCPU IP（ARM、RISC‑V 等）に関する知識・評価経験  論理合成、タイミング解析、電力解析等の設計フローに関する経験  RTLデザイン(VerilogHDL/VHDL設計、検証、論理合成)の経験  英語による技術文書の作成および技術的なディスカッションの実務経験  日本語：ビジネスレベルでの会話・コミュニケーションが可能な方  英語：実務での使用（読み書き・会話）に抵抗のない方    【WANT】    CPUの設計経験  実装経験(タイミング設計、レイアウト)  英語：日常会話ができる (TOEIC 600点程度)      ルネサスは、「To Make Our Lives Easier（人々の暮らしをより豊かで快適にする）」というPurposeのもと、組込み半導体ソリューションを提供するグローバル企業です。世界30か国以上で活躍する21,000人を超えるエンジニアや課題解決のプロフェッショナルとともに、自動車、産業、インフラ、IoT分野における世界最先端のテクノロジー開発に携わり、より安全で、健康的で、環境にやさしく、スマートな未来の実現に貢献しています。      ルネサスでは、「TAGIE（Transparent、Agile、Global、Innovative、Entrepreneurial）」を企業文化の中核としています。TAGIEは、私たちの働き方や成長のあり方、そしてPurposeの実現に向けた取り組みを支える共通の価値観です。この協調的な精神と挑戦するマインドセットが、半導体技術を通じた産業の変革と、世界中の人々の暮らしへの貢献を可能にしています。      私たちは、競争力のある報酬制度に加え、充実した福利厚生をご用意しています。福利厚生の詳細については、選考プロセスの中でご案内いたします。      私たちとともに未来を創造する挑戦に、ぜひ参加しませんか。皆さまからのご応募をお待ちしております。

This position is in CMSD Korea, which is part of Renesas’ Analog & Connectivity organization.  The CMSD R&D team develops and industrializes highly configurable mixed-signal products for a wide range of applications, including but not limited to consumer, communication, computing, data center, industrial, and automotive applications. CMSD team is the pioneer and dominant market leader of the highly successful GreenPAK family of products. CMSD team is continuously expanding our product portfolio that includes high performance analog IP’s, DC-DC, and FPGA. 
    Understand the transistor- and system- level architecture.  Ensure the performance of the high precision analog block to meet process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) variations.  Contribute to the high-performance silicon-proven IP development.  Collaborate with digital engineers on trimming and control for analog circuit.  Guide to layout engineer to minimize the layout effects.  Perform hands-on evaluation of IPs to use equipment like multimeter and oscilloscope.  Collaborate with test engineering to ensure adequate test coverage.  Analyze the ATE & CHZ data to validate product specification.  Interface and Support with various teams in design view.  Participate in root cause analysis of performance and functional issues.  Modeling of analog and mixed-signal circuits for top-level testbench.       1. M.D. or Ph.D in EE semiconductor design by using CMOS 
2. Strong knowledge in design and layout of analog and mixed-signal circuit design and architecture with various blocks such as amplifiers, comparator, bandgap, voltage- and current- generator, oscillator, regulator, data converter, digital logic, etc. 
3. Strong background of analog and digital IC design, layout, tools, process, measurement. 
4. Strong understanding of Mixed-Signal design flow and Top-Down development methodology for optimizing PPA (Power, Performance, Area) 
5. Ability to understand and prove the difference between hand calculation and simulation. 
6. Experience with simulation tools (Cadence, Verilog, Python etc.) 
7. Experience in semiconductor reliability and failure analysis. 
8. Clearly explain the operation of circuits and systems 
9. Documenting accurately and clearly analysis & conclusion 
10. Strongly self-motivated and open mind with team working skills. 
11. Strong English Communication with Design, Characterization, Test Engineering, technical writing team from various countries. Renesas is seeking a highly skilled Senior Manager of Field Applications Engineering to lead strategic technical engagement with our most important AI and hyperscaler customers. This role leads a high-performance team of power supply FAEs supporting AI accelerators, servers, and networking platforms that are critical to Renesas’ long-term growth.  This is a senior player/coach position. The role balances hands-on ownership of customer power programs with leadership and development of a growing FAE organization. Success requires deep power electronics expertise, strong customer credibility, and the ability to scale technical execution across multiple strategic accounts.   Key Responsibilities    Player/Coach Responsibilities (Hands-On Technical Leadership)   Serve as the senior technical interface for strategic datacenter accounts, driving system-level power architecture engagements from early concept through production.  Provide expert leadership on digital multiphase power, power modules, and server-class power delivery architectures supporting AI accelerators, CPUs, and networking platforms.  Personally engage in the most complex customer programs, including architecture reviews, schematic and layout feedback, validation planning, bring-up, power sequencing analysis, transient response evaluation, and debug.  Rapidly troubleshoot complex power issues using lab instrumentation including oscilloscopes, current probes, electronic loads, and transient analysis tools.  Lead technical escalations with internal engineering teams to ensure rapid, high-quality resolution of customer issues.  Deliver high-quality customer-facing materials such as validation results, program updates, technical summaries, and program closure reports.   People & Team Leadership   Lead, mentor, and develop a team of power supply FAEs supporting strategic AI and hyperscaler customers.  Coach FAEs on system-level power thinking, executive communication, and sound technical judgment in complex customer environments.  Build onboarding and training plans for new college graduates and early-career FAEs, ensuring readiness for lab work and customer-facing engagements.  Conduct performance reviews and support career development across the team.  Guide resource allocation across accounts, balancing customer priorities, program risk, and team bandwidth.  Establish a high-performance culture with clear standards for ownership, technical rigor, and execution quality. Hold the team accountable to outcomes and model the behaviors expected through disciplined, high-impact customer engagement.   Customer, Program & Strategy Leadership   Own technical program execution for top datacenter customers, spanning AI accelerators, server platforms, and high-performance networking systems.  Partner closely with Sales and GAM leadership to align customer priorities, program sequencing, and allocation of FAE resources.  Maintain program visibility through clear tracking of milestones, risks, validation status, and next-step actions.  Provide concise and actionable technical updates to senior leadership.  Collaborate with Product Line and Marketing teams to translate strategic customer power requirements into product feedback and roadmap influence.  Champion field insights related to next-generation power architectures, digital multiphase solutions, and module-based system power.  Coordinate technical handoffs and shared engagements across global FAE teams.    Required   Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a related technical field.  Significant prior experience as a Field Applications Engineer with hands-on responsibility for power supply or power management products.  8+ years of experience in power electronics, digital multiphase power delivery, server or AI platform power, or related hardware systems.  Deep technical expertise in power modules, digital multiphase controllers, VRMs, and high-current, low-voltage conversion for datacenter platforms.  Strong lab-based debug skills including use of oscilloscopes, current probes, electronic loads, and transient response analysis.  Demonstrated ability to interface directly with customers on complex power topics and drive issues to closure.  2+ years of people leadership experience in a team lead, supervisory, managerial, or equivalent player/coach role.  Strong communication skills with the ability to translate complex technical concepts to customer, executive, and internal audiences.   Preferred   Experience supporting hyperscale datacenter customers such as cloud service providers or AI accelerator companies.  Expertise in system-level power architecture for AI or ML accelerators, CPUs, or high-end networking platforms.  Familiarity with PMBus, telemetry systems, and digitally controlled multiphase power solutions.  Proven ability to manage multiple high-priority programs simultaneously in fast-moving customer environments.  Demonstrated success developing early-career engineers and building high-performance technical teams.  Strong cross-functional leadership experience working with Product Line, Marketing, Sales, or Systems Engineering organizations.    Why This Role Matters   Power delivery is a defining constraint and differentiator for AI and hyperscaler platforms. This role operates at the intersection of customer execution, power architecture leadership, and long-term strategy. The Senior Manager, Field Applications Engineering – Strategic Accounts (Power) will directly shape how Renesas is perceived by its most strategic customers and materially impact our ability to win and scale next-generation datacenter platforms.     The expected annual pay range for this position is $158-$222K. This position is also eligible for bonus opportunities. Please note that final offer amount will be dependent on geographic location, applicable experience, and skillset of the candidate. ・英語による技術資料読解能力     ルネサスは、「To Make Our Lives Easier（人々の暮らしをより豊かで快適にする）」というPurposeのもと、組込み半導体ソリューションを提供するグローバル企業です。世界30か国以上で活躍する21,000人を超えるエンジニアや課題解決のプロフェッショナルとともに、自動車、産業、インフラ、IoT分野における世界最先端のテクノロジー開発に携わり、より安全で、健康的で、環境にやさしく、スマートな未来の実現に貢献しています。      ルネサスでは、「TAGIE（Transparent、Agile、Global、Innovative、Entrepreneurial）」を企業文化の中核としています。TAGIEは、私たちの働き方や成長のあり方、そしてPurposeの実現に向けた取り組みを支える共通の価値観です。この協調的な精神と挑戦するマインドセットが、半導体技術を通じた産業の変革と、世界中の人々の暮らしへの貢献を可能にしています。      私たちは、競争力のある報酬制度に加え、充実した福利厚生をご用意しています。福利厚生の詳細については、選考プロセスの中でご案内いたします。      私たちとともに未来を創造する挑戦に、ぜひ参加しませんか。皆さまからのご応募をお待ちしております。

As a Senior Field Applications Engineer (FAE) you will play a major role in the expansion of our market-leading digital products (MCUs & SoCs), analog and power by providing outstanding application engineering support to our customers. You will also play a key role in the definition of the next generation of Renesas Automotive Products working closely to the customer engineering teams and to Renesas application engineering and marketing teams.  In your new role you will: 
•    Drive the design-in activities of the complete product portfolio in automotive applications such as IVI, ADAS, xEV, Vehicle Controls etc. working with Automotive OEM customers. 
•    Define new products in close cooperation with our innovative customers and our internal technical marketing and applications teams. 
•    Act as a technical interface and consult our customers during the development of all automotive applications with particular focus on OEMs. 
•    Derive customer system requirements and market trends to develop system value propositions together with internal interfaces (Product Marketers, Application Engineers, System Architects). 
•    Build a good understanding of different product architectures and partner ecosystem to suggest/guide customers, to arrive at an optimal system design. 
•    Actively manage projects together with the Sales and Marketing departments to achieve design-in targets for the complete Renesas automotive product portfolio. 
•    Establish and maintain excellent relationships with the customer engineering departments with particular focus on OEMs. 
•    Proactively connect with global cross-functional teams, expand your internal network, and share your experience to drive global business expansion. 
•    Lead technical discussions with System Architects and Application Engineering experts to jointly define application roadmaps and product technical requirements. 
•    Collaborate internally with Application Engineers and Product Marketers and externally with local and global partners to develop documentation (fighting guides, application notes, whitepapers) and system demonstrators combining software and hardware. 
•    Perform measurements in our laboratory within the scope of actual customer projects. 
•    Present Renesas’ technologies, products, and applications in technical seminars. We are seeking a Powertrain Design Engineer to lead the development of test vehicles supporting our high-current BCD (Bipolar-CMOS-DMOS) and low-voltage GaN power process and product portfolios. This role owns test vehicle definition, circuit and layout design, and characterization planning from concept through silicon bring-up, working closely with process development, product engineering, and applications teams. The ideal candidate has hands-on experience designing power devices and circuits at both the IC and module level, and is fluent in the power topologies these test vehicles are ultimately intended to support.   Key Responsibilities    Define, design, and drive execution of test vehicles (TVs) for high-current BCD and LV GaN process technologies, including device test structures, scaled power stages, and full-function demonstration circuits.  Translate process capability targets and product roadmap requirements into test vehicle architecture and specifications.  Design and simulate power stage circuits (e.g., synchronous buck/boost, multiphase, half-bridge/DrMOS, gate drivers) used to validate device performance under realistic switching and thermal conditions.  Select and characterize power devices (LDMOS, trench MOSFETs, LV GaN HEMTs, Schottky/sync rectifiers) for inclusion in test structures, working with device/process engineering on layout-dependent tradeoffs (RDS(ON), Qg, breakdown voltage, SOA).  Perform IC-level layout and design for test structures, including parasitic-aware layout for switch nodes, current sensing, and gate drive paths.  Extend designs to module/package level as needed — co-design of power stages with packaging, magnetics, and PCB layout for evaluation boards and system-level test vehicles.  Develop test and characterization plans covering DC parametrics, switching performance, efficiency, transient response, and voltage/current stress margins (including switch-node ringing and abs-max validation).  Lead or support silicon bring-up, debug, and correlation of measured results against simulation and design targets.  Collaborate cross-functionally with process integration, reliability, product/applications engineering, and test engineering to close the loop from process split data to product-ready specifications.  Document design methodology, test vehicle results, and characterization data to support technology qualification and product development decisions. Some markets you join. This one you help build.  AI compute is outgrowing the ground. As GPU and AI-class systems move into space and other demanding high-reliability settings, the power electronics that feed them have to survive radiation, wide temperature swings, and years of operation with no chance of a service call, at volumes well beyond anything the space industry has produced before. Standard commercial-grade parts cannot meet that bar. Renesas can, and we are opening a new high-reliability (Hi-Rel) growth area to do it: radiation-cognizant power management built on our power portfolio and decades of Hi-Rel heritage.  We are looking for a Staff Business Development Specialist to lead the way into this market. This is a market-creation role, not a territory to maintain. You will find where the real opportunities are, build the customer base from the first conversation, and turn early technical engagements into design wins. You will sit across the table from the GPU and AI-silicon vendors, space-systems primes, and hyperscale operators defining this field, and you will work alongside our product, design, applications, and sales teams to turn those relationships into revenue. If you want your fingerprints on an industry while it is still taking shape, this is that job.  Responsibilities  In this role, you will:  • Identify, pursue, and capture new business in a market Renesas is entering for the first time, from first contact through design-in and production.  • Own senior technical and commercial relationships across the target accounts, from AI-silicon vendors to space-systems primes to hyperscale operators.  • Size the addressable and serviceable market, and build the go-to-market plan that prioritizes accounts, applications, and timing.  • Shape customer requirements early, respond to RFIs and RFPs, and lead proposal development in coordination with product and applications teams.  • Develop pricing and value strategy for radiation-cognizant solutions relative to commodity and fully rad-hard alternatives.  • Run competitive intelligence on incumbent power and Hi-Rel suppliers, and use it to sharpen positioning and roadmap input.  • Support executive reviews and corporate funding proposals with market data, revenue projections, and a defensible business case.  • Work cross-functionally with design, applications, product marketing, and regional sales to align the portfolio with customer needs and to drive design-ins to closure.   • 10 or more years in business development, strategic sales, or product marketing, in semiconductors, power management, aerospace and defense, or high-reliability and space markets.  • Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering or a related field. An MBA is a plus.  • A track record of opening new markets and closing design-ins or partnerships, ideally where the market did not yet exist.  • Direct experience working at, or selling into, GPU and AI-accelerator vendors or hyperscale operators is a major plus.  • The ability to hold technical discussions on power delivery and mixed-signal design with customer engineers, and to translate them into commercial strategy.  • Strong proposal, negotiation, and executive-communication skills.  • Comfort operating in an export-controlled, high-reliability environment.  • Willingness to travel to customers and Renesas sites.  • An independent operator who works effectively across US and Japan-based leadership. We are looking for an experienced and visionary System Architect to serve as Renesas' global technical leader for Drone and UAV applications. This individual will define and drive end-to-end system architectures for next-generation UAV platforms while identifying emerging market opportunities, shaping solution roadmaps, and promoting differentiated semiconductor and software solutions.  You will act as the primary technical authority for Drone & UAV applications, bridging customer requirements, ecosystem needs, aviation regulations, and semiconductor product engineering. Beyond architecture definition, you will help guide solution strategy, ecosystem engagement, reference platform development, and semiconductor adoption across industrial, commercial and defense UAV markets.  Key Responsibilities   Define and own end-to-end system architectures for industrial and/or defense drone and UAV applications, covering flight control, mission computing, sensing, propulsion, power, connectivity, and ground-control interfaces.  Translate customer use cases and mission requirements into system, hardware, software, performance, safety, security, and interface requirements.  Drive HW/SW partitioning across MCUs, MPUs/SoCs, AI accelerators, programmable logic, sensors, connectivity devices, power electronics, and actuators.  Define architectures for flight control, sensor fusion, navigation, positioning, stabilization, autonomous mission execution, obstacle detection, and collision avoidance.  Specify and integrate sensing solutions such as IMUs, GNSS/RTK, cameras, radar, LiDAR, ultrasonic sensors, barometric sensors, and environmental sensors.  Define compute architectures for edge AI, computer vision, visual-inertial odometry, SLAM, object detection, tracking, and autonomous decision-making.  Develop robust communication architectures covering command and control, telemetry, payload data, remote identification, vehicle-to-vehicle links, cloud connectivity, and ground-control systems.  Define power and propulsion architectures, including battery management, power conversion and distribution, motor control, energy optimization, thermal management, and fault monitoring.  Ensure safety, reliability, cybersecurity, redundancy, fault containment, degraded-operation modes, and fail-safe behaviors are designed into the system architecture.  Collaborate closely with Product Groups, system architects, hardware, software, AI, connectivity, power, motor-control, security, and validation teams to deliver cohesive semiconductor-based solutions.  Support product definition and roadmaps by identifying UAV system requirements, technology gaps, architectural trade-offs, and opportunities for differentiated semiconductor and software solutions.  Guide and review system design, implementation, integration, verification, validation, and flight-test activities across the development lifecycle.  Engage with drone OEMs, technology partners, research institutes, and ecosystem providers to understand requirements, support architecture discussions, and accelerate design-in activities.  Support customer engagements by explaining system concepts, design choices, performance trade-offs, integration guidelines, and reference solution capabilities.  Monitor market trends, evolving regulations, emerging technologies, and competitive solutions, and translate insights into application strategies and architectures.  Influence product and technology roadmaps by translating evolving UAV market requirements into strategic semiconductor investment opportunities.  Contribute to reference architectures, evaluation platforms, proofs of concept, application notes, and reusable solution building blocks for multiple UAV platforms.  Provide technical mentoring, design reviews, and domain guidance to internal engineering, application, field, and product teams.     Master’s or Ph.D. degree in Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Computer Engineering, Robotics, Mechatronics, Systems Engineering, or a related field.  8+ years of experience in drone, UAV, aerospace, robotics, autonomous-system, or embedded-system development, with significant responsibility for system architecture and integration.  Systems Engineer in the development of industrial and/or defense drone platforms. Proven track record as a System Architect, Chief Engineer, Technical Lead, or Senior  Hands-on experience contributing to at least one UAV platform through architecture, development, system integration, verification, flight testing, and product deployment.  Deep understanding of UAV architectures, including flight controllers, mission computers, avionics, propulsion, power systems, payloads, communication links, and ground-control systems.  Strong knowledge of embedded systems, MCUs, MPUs/SoCs, real-time software, embedded Linux, RTOS platforms, and heterogeneous computing architectures.  Strong experience in flight control, estimation, sensor fusion, navigation, GNSS/RTK, perception, autonomy, or other safety- and mission-critical UAV functions.    Nice to Have    Experience with PX4, ArduPilot, ROS 2, MAVLink, DDS, or comparable UAV and robotics software frameworks.  Familiarity with aviation development and safety practices, EASA or FAA UAV regulations, Remote ID, BVLOS operations, and relevant standards such as DO-178C, DO-254, ARP4754A, or ARP4761.  Experience with edge AI, computer vision, SLAM, visual-inertial odometry, radar or LiDAR perception, and AI accelerator platforms.  Background in electric propulsion, motor control, battery management, power conversion, or high-efficiency power electronics for aerial systems.  Experience with cybersecurity, secure communications, GNSS resilience, anti-jamming, or system-level threat analysis.  Knowledge of simulation, model-based systems engineering, software-in-the-loop, hardware-in-the-loop, and digital-twin environments.  Experience supporting third-party assessments, flight approvals, certification, or regulatory compliance activities. High technical ownership and influence on product strategy, architecture, ecosystem development, and customer success.
