## Senior FP&A Analyst

Location: Toronto, ON
Work Model: Hybrid, flexible office attendance as needed

Reporting to the VP, FP&A, you will support the CFO and senior leadership team by transforming complex financial and operational data into clear, actionable recommendations. • Deliver scenario analyses, profitability assessments, and ROI evaluations that support investment, pricing, and resource allocation decisions.

• Build trusted relationships across the organization while influencing decisions through data-driven recommendations.

## Summary

## Responsibilities

## Perform Incoming, In-Process, and Final Inspections

• Conduct inspections of raw materials, components, and finished products in accordance with quality procedures and control plans.

• Review and approve Certificates of Analysis (COAs) for raw materials and maintain associated records.

• Prepare and handle fittings for inspection and third-party non-destructive examination (NDE) testing.

• Verify compliance with specifications and standards and determine product acceptance status.

• Conduct random inspections of products and measuring equipment and report non-conforming conditions.

## Execute Quality Control Testing

• Perform quality control testing for incoming and in-process materials in accordance with established procedures and industry standards, including ASTM requirements.

• Generate accurate test reports and maintain testing schedules established by the Quality Supervisor.

• Support achievement of performance targets including attainment and testing cycle times.

• Escalate non-conforming test results by initiating NCRs and requesting engineering review when required.

## Drive Non-Conformance Reporting and Quality Improvement

• Create and manage Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs) within the business system for products, processes, and failed tests.

• Identify product defects through routine inspections and provide observations and recommendations.

• Communicate inspection findings and quality concerns to the Quality Supervisor and production teams.

• Support root cause analysis and continuous improvement efforts.

## Support Quality Management Systems and Audits

• Participate in Quality Management System (QMS) improvement initiatives.

• Attend production meetings and provide feedback on NCR trends, first-time quality performance, and quality-related priorities.

• Support internal and external audits and maintain compliance with quality standards and procedures.

• Assist with updating inspection and testing procedures as needed.

## Maintain Documentation and Records

• Review, update, and manage quality-related procedures and inspection documentation.

• Maintain production and quality records to support traceability and compliance requirements.

• Ensure inspection and testing documentation is complete, accurate, and readily accessible.

## Promote Safety and Continuous Improvement

• Actively participate in health, safety, environmental, volunteer, and continuous improvement initiatives.

• Support a safe working environment by following established procedures and promoting safe work practices.

• Contribute to ongoing operational and quality improvements throughout the facility.

## Qualifications, Education, and Certifications

• High School Diploma or equivalent (required)

• College Diploma (preferred)

• Knowledge of ANSI inspection levels and Acceptable Quality Limit (AQL) methodologies. (preferred)

• Familiarity with ANSI/ASQC Z1.4 or ISO 2859-1 standards. (preferred)

## Required Experience

• 1 to 3 years of experience in manufacturing quality inspection or quality control environment.

• Experience performing inspections, testing, and documentation within a manufacturing setting.

• Experience in pipe, polymer, composite, or related manufacturing environments. (preferred)

## Technical Knowledge and Skills

• Basic knowledge of quality management systems, inspection methodologies, and testing practices.

• Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and quality standards.

• Proficiency with measurement tools and inspection equipment.

• Basic understanding of ISO 9001 and API Q1 quality requirements.

• Strong documentation, reporting, and organizational skills.

• Ability to perform regular manual inspection activities requiring prolonged standing, walking, visual concentration, and handling materials up to 50 lbs while wearing appropriate PPE.

## Position Overview:

As an R&D Nuclear Engineer specializing in Computational Materials, you’ll serve as a senior technical authority focused on advancing high‑fidelity, multiphysics simulations that underpin the design, qualification, and optimization of nuclear fuel systems. This role integrates deep expertise in materials science, thermomechanical behavior, chemical interaction modeling, and nuclear fuel phenomena with sophisticated computational model development. The engineer will lead the creation, improvement, and application of fuel performance models within BWXT’s fuel performance code suites and other high‑fidelity simulation tools. Core responsibilities include designing robust computational workflows, developing physics‑based material models, enhancing code capabilities, and driving innovation to support next‑generation nuclear fuel concepts.

## Location:

Remote or on-site at the BWXT Innovation Campus site in Lynchburg, VA.

## Your Day to Day as a R&D Nuclear Engineer - Computational Materials:

• Lead development and application of advanced multiphysics models for nuclear fuel performance, including thermal, mechanical, chemical, and irradiation-driven phenomena.

• Develop and implement constitutive models describing fuel material behavior, microstructural evolution, degradation mechanisms, and coupled thermo‑mechanical‑chemical interactions.

• Conduct high‑fidelity analyses of nuclear fuel systems under normal operating, transient, and off‑normal conditions.

• Guide verification, validation, benchmarking, and uncertainty quantification for modeling tools, with emphasis on fuel performance predictions.

• Build and refine scalable computational methodologies suitable for high‑performance computing environments.

• Collaborate with materials scientists, fuel performance engineers, and software developers to integrate modeling capabilities across simulation workflows.

• Prepare rigorous technical documentation, research reports, and contributions to regulatory, customer, and R&D deliverables.

• Mentor junior staff and provide strategic input on long‑term modeling and simulation initiatives.

## Required Qualifications:

• A Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or Physics is required.

• A minimum of seven (7) years of relevant experience is required; an advanced degree may be considered in lieu of experience.

• Demonstrated experience with multiphysics modeling, finite element analysis, or computational materials science tools.

• In depth experience and understanding of nuclear fuel materials behavior, including thermo‑mechanical response, irradiation effects, and chemical interactions.

• Proficiency in scientific programming languages and engineering computation (FORTRAN, Python, C, C++, or similar).

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills with a history of impactful technical contributions.

• Must be a U.S. citizen.

• Must be able to obtain and maintain a U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) or Department of Defense (DOD) security clearance, whichever is required.

## Preferred Qualifications:

• Thorough experience using MOOSE/BISON or similar multiphysics nuclear fuel performance codes.

• In depth experience with oxide, nitride, carbide (UO₂, UN, UC), metallic (U‑Zr, U-Pu-Zr, U‑Mo), and advanced fuel concepts (TRISO, ATF coatings, SiC cladding, composite systems).

• Direct experience developing within the MOOSE framework and customizing BISON-based applications.

• Experience leading software development projects in scientific or multiphysics environments.

• Experience with HPC environments, parallel computing, and performance optimization.

• Ability to design and execute R&D experiments or modeling campaigns to test new fuel concepts or material behaviors.

• Experience with verification, validation, sensitivity studies and uncertainty quantification method development associated with fuel qualification.

## What We Offer:

• Competitive salary and benefits package, including health, dental, and retirement plans.

• Flexible work schedules and paid time off to promote a healthy work-life balance.

• Professional development opportunities, including mentorship programs and sponsorship for continuing education.

• An inclusive atmosphere that celebrates new perspectives and supports collaboration between different generations.

• The chance to be part of a mission-driven organization making a positive impact on the future of energy.

• Opportunities for continuous learning and training to grow throughout your career!

A U.S.-based company, BWXT is a Fortune 1000 and Defense News Top 100 manufacturing and engineering innovator that provides safe and effective nuclear solutions for global security, clean energy, environmental restoration, nuclear medicine and space exploration. With more than 7,800 employees, BWXT has 14 major operating sites in the U.S., Canada and the U.K. We are the sole manufacturer of naval nuclear reactors for U.S. submarines and aircraft carriers. Our company supplies precision manufactured components, services and fuel for the commercial nuclear power industry across four continents. Our joint ventures provide environmental restoration and operations management at a dozen U.S. Department of Energy and NASA facilities. BWXT’s technology is driving advances in medical radioisotope production in North America and microreactors for various defense and space applications. For more information, visit www.bwxt.com. Follow us on LinkedIn, X, Facebook and Instagram.

## Welcome to BWXT

We believe in empowering our employees and cultivating a dynamic workplace that fosters growth and collaboration. Whether you’re an experienced professional or just starting your career, you'll find opportunities to challenge yourself, learn from seasoned experts, and contribute to nuclear innovation. We require a diverse range of skills to support our work in the markets that drive our business and welcome candidates from all backgrounds and life stages who are passionate about making a difference.

## Position Overview:

This position serves as a key HR partner by providing daily support, guidance, and engagement to employees and leaders across the site. The role manages full‑cycle hiring needs, conducts employee relations investigations, and ensures consistent application of policies and employment regulations. It also maintains accurate and confidential employee records, and supports a variety of employee events and compliance activities.

This position supports a safety and quality driven, 24-7 manufacturing operation and requires the ability and availability to occasionally work the adjusted schedule. Variations to normal work hours may include, but are not limited to, support of early morning meetings, engagement with the shop floor during 2nd shift evening operations, scheduled plant initiatives, unplanned after-hours investigations and pre-planned weekend employee events.

## Location:

On-site in Mt. Vernon, IN

## Your Day-to-Day as a Human Resources Generalist:

• Provide daily HR support on the shop floor by engaging with employees, responding promptly to questions, and addressing concerns as soon as they arise.

• Partner with leadership and Talent Acquisition to deliver full-cycle support for the site’s hiring needs.

• Advise employees and managers on interpreting policies, guidelines, procedures, laws, and other regulatory requirements.

• Conduct employee relations investigations that prioritize factual accuracy, adherence to legal and policy requirements, and timely resolution.

• Assist with employee events, including benefits enrollment, policy training, organization-wide meetings, career fairs and employee recognition events.

• Maintain regulatory compliance by routinely verifying that all required legal and ethics postings are current and properly displayed.

• Manage the maintenance, integrity and confidentiality of new hire files and records.

• Collaborate closely with front-line leaders and employees to improve working relationships, boost morale, and strengthen productivity and retention.

## Required Minimum Qualifications:

• A Bachelor’s Degree in human resources, business, or a closely related field.

• Minimum of one year of HR experience that includes hands-on work in staffing, benefits, compensation, employee relations, and employment law compliance.

• Ability to work fully onsite at BWXT’s Mt. Vernon, IN office location.

• Proven ability to deliver strong customer service while maintaining strict adherence to legal and policy requirements.

• Proven ability to manage time effectively and balance multiple competing priorities.

• Demonstrated intermediate proficiency in Microsoft Outlook, PowerPoint, and Word. Advanced Excel proficiency with the ability to produce required business reporting.

• Ability to communicate effectively at all organizational levels and collaborate successfully with cross-functional teams.

• Must be a U.S. citizen.

• Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a Department of Energy (DOE) security clearance.

## Preferred Qualifications:

• SHRM Certification

## What We Offer:

• Competitive salary and benefits package, including health, dental, and retirement plans.

• Flexible work schedules and paid time off to promote a healthy work-life balance.

• Professional development opportunities, including mentorship programs and sponsorship for continuing education.

• An inclusive atmosphere that celebrates new perspectives and supports collaboration between different generations.

• The chance to be part of a mission-driven organization making a positive impact on the future of energy.

• Opportunities for continuous learning and training to grow throughout your career!

Position Overview:
The Licensing Manager leads all aspects of license application development, including initial regulatory program requirements for a uranium enrichment facility, overseeing preparation, coordination, and execution of the site’s NRC license application. This role serves as the facility’s primary regulatory interface, ensuring compliance with applicable NRC regulations while directing cross-functional technical, safety, and operational contributions.

## Location:

On-site in Oak Ridge, Tennessee

## Your Day to Day as a Licensing Manager:

• Leads a multidisciplinary licensing team, providing direction, coaching, and performance oversight.

• Acts as a liaison with the NRC, other regulatory bodies and local stakeholders, overseeing correspondence, inspections, and regulatory engagement planning.

• Coordinates with internal engineering, safety, operations, and executive leadership to ensure alignment of licensing strategy and technical deliverables.

• Manages the development, submission, and maintenance of the facility’s licensing basis, including license application content, amendment requests, exemption requests, and responses to NRC requests for additional information.

• Manages pre-application strategy, license application submittals, and implementation of regulatory commitments.

• Represents the facility during NRC inspections, audits, rulemaking reviews, and enforcement interactions.

• Demonstrates leadership in cross-functional teams including safety analysis, fire protection, configuration management, and procurement QA.

• Directs development of NRC license application materials, including safety analysis, radiation protection, material control and accounting, criticality safety, and emergency preparedness elements.

• Manages regulatory engagement plans, pre-application interactions, and formal review processes.

• Prepares, reviews, and submits regulatory correspondence such as amendment requests, exemptions, application supplements, and RAI responses.

• Reviews and comments on NRC rulemaking activities relevant to uranium enrichment and fuel cycle licensing.

• Maintains the facility’s licensing basis and associated change control programs.

• Leads resolution of licensing-related issues and oversee implementation of corrective action program items.

• Ensures accuracy, completeness, and version control for licensing documentation.

• Manages licensing schedules, deliverables, and milestones.

• Coordinates with engineering and design teams to ensure regulatory requirements are integrated into design development and change management.

## Required Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering, nuclear sciences, regulatory affairs, or a related technical discipline.

• At least 5 years of nuclear industry regulatory or licensing experience.

• Minimum 2 years of supervisory or team leadership experience.

• Working knowledge of NRC regulations including 10 CFR Parts 50, 52, 70, and 74.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to interact effectively with regulators.

• Must be a U.S. citizen.

• Must be able to obtain and maintain a U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) clearance.

## Preferred Qualifications:

• Master’s degree in engineering, nuclear science, regulatory affairs, or related discipline.

• 7–10+ years of nuclear licensing experience, particularly with fuel cycle facilities or Part 70 licensees.

• Experience with NRC change authority evaluations (10 CFR 70.72, 50.59, 95.19).

• Prior leadership experience in NRC application development and technical review processes.

• Experience with criticality safety, environmental compliance, and emergency planning frameworks for enrichment facilities.

## What We Offer:

• Competitive salary and benefits package, including health, dental, and retirement plans.

• Flexible work schedules and paid time off to promote a healthy work-life balance.

• Professional development opportunities, including mentorship programs and sponsorship for continuing education.

• An inclusive atmosphere that celebrates new perspectives and supports collaboration between different generations.

• The chance to be part of a mission-driven organization making a positive impact on the future of energy.

• Opportunities for continuous learning and training to grow throughout your career!

## Position Overview:

We are excited to offer an exceptional opportunity for a Welding Engineering Intern to join our innovative team, where you will play a vital role in supporting welding engineering projects and enhancing operational efficiencies. As an intern, you will assist the Welding Engineering Team with a range of responsibilities, including learning and executing basic shop floor and contract welding duties, leading 5S and process improvement initiatives, and aiding in welding procedure development. You will also conduct system audits, apply your knowledge to support troubleshooting and operations, and contribute to documentation and analysis of welding metrics. This internship provides a valuable opportunity to gain hands-on experience in a collaborative environment while making meaningful contributions to our welding processes.

## Location:

On-site in Mount Vernon, IN

## Your Day to Day as a Welding Engineer Intern:

• Learn and carryout basic functions of shop floor and contract welding engineering duties

• Lead 5S/process improvement projects relating to specific shop operation jobs

• Assist with performance of welding procedure development and interpretations

• Perform welding operation and system audits

• Apply knowledge of welding processes to support shop floor operations and troubleshooting of welding equipment and operations

• Documentation and support of operational improvements such as the following:

• Creation of job specific aids, weld instructions, or checklists

• Carryout operational efficiency projects (Individual & Team Based (Multi-discipline)

• Support data collection and analysis for weld metrics

• Ensure welding processes meet customer specifications.

• Ensure welding operations meet customer specifications and good work practices.

## Required Qualifications:

• Must be enrolled full time in a Welding Engineering program.

• Must have enough credits to be at least at sophomore status

• Prior internship experience is preferred but not required.

• Experience or knowledge with basic arc welding processes such as GTAW, SMAW, SAW, and GMAW welding. Robotics/Automated process knowledge is preferred but not required.

• Proficient in fundamental computer skills (Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.)

• Strong technical problem-solving abilities and interpersonal skills

• Excellent technical writing and verbal communication skills

• Must be a U.S. citizen

## Preferred Qualifications:

• ABET accreditation is preferred.

• Prior internships and/or experience in a heavy manufacturing environment is preferred.

• Robotics/Automated process knowledge is preferred.

## What We Offer:

• A competitively paid internship experience.

• A housing stipend for interns whose home of record is more than 50 miles from Mt. Vernon, IN.

• An inclusive atmosphere that celebrates new perspectives and supports collaboration between different generations.

• The chance to be part of a mission-driven organization making a positive impact on the future of energy.

• Opportunities for continuous learning and training!

## Position Overview:

As our Director of Quality Assurance you will report directly to the site General Manager, as a senior staff member. You'll be responsible to lead a team of managers that direct quality control inspectors and NDT examiners, quality assurance engineers, auditors, and administration professionals. You will own site compliance to our quality management system and be responsible for overseeing internal root cause and corrective action programs. The successful candidate must have exceptional communication skills necessary to motivate their team and create a strong collaboration culture with other departments. You'll also need to have a strong drive for continuous improvement so that quality personnel are efficient and the business evaluates and adopts the best emerging technologies to improve inspection and assurance activities. You'll also be expected to present quality performance and initiatives to executives and senior customer stakeholders with transparency and confidence.

## Location:

On-site in Mt. Vernon, Indiana

## Your Challenge as Director of Quality Assurance:

• Direct and improve the daily operations of all quality functions to support a 24/7 production environment

• Lead, mentor, and coach a team of quality managers to maximize their effectiveness and grow their careers

• Ensure a fair and transparent work environment for quality personnel that maximizes employee satisfaction and achieves business objectives

• Be the direct liaison with customer and government Quality Assurance management representatives

• Assure the maintenance of Quality auditing and inspection activities

• Revise and maintain Quality Management System instructions and procedures

• Establish quality specific training programs and initiatives for the site

• Facilitate a learning organization driving down escapes, rework and scrap by generating sound root causes, corrective actions and preventative actions

• Evaluate, test, promote, and adopt emerging technologies that support compliance to customer standards and improve the efficiency and accuracy of NDT

• Assure that product quality levels are maintained

## Required Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Science or Technical field

• Minimum of ten (10) years experience in Quality Assurance, Engineering, and/or related disciplines

• Minimum of five (5) years management experience

• Deep understanding of data management, business analytics, and performance metrics

• Exceptional communications and collaboration skills

• Must be a US Citizen with the ability to obtain a DOE "L" security clearance

## Preferred Qualifications:

• Submarine Safety, Naval Nuclear and/or Commercial Nuclear quality experience

• Diversified background in machining, welding, fabrication, and NDE

• Working knowledge of Defense and ASME Code Specifications for pressure vessels

## What We Offer:

• Competitive salary and benefits package, including health, dental, and retirement plans.

• Paid time off to promote a healthy work-life balance.

• Professional development opportunities, including mentorship programs and sponsorship for continuing education.

• An inclusive atmosphere that celebrates new perspectives and supports collaboration between different generations.

• The chance to be part of a mission-driven organization making a positive impact on the future of energy.

• Opportunities for continuous learning and training to grow throughout your career!

Position Overview:
The EH&S Manager – Enrichment Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for the Environmental, Health, and Safety (EH&S) function supporting BWXT's uranium enrichment operations. This role is responsible for developing, implementing, and continuously improving comprehensive environmental, occupational health, industrial safety, waste management, and regulatory compliance programs that enable safe, reliable, and compliant operations across the Centrifuge Manufacturing Development Facility (CMDF), Centrifuge Manufacturing Facility (CMF), and future enrichment-related operations.

Operating within a highly regulated environment, the EH&S Manager serves as a trusted advisor to operational leadership, ensuring safety is integrated into every aspect of planning, manufacturing, engineering, maintenance, commissioning, and facility operations. The position champions a proactive safety culture built on operational discipline, human performance improvement (HPI), continuous risk reduction, and environmental stewardship while supporting the organization's mission of delivering critical national security capabilities.

The successful candidate will balance strategic planning with day-to-day execution, driving measurable improvements in safety performance, regulatory compliance, employee engagement, and operational excellence.

## Location:

On-site in Oak Ridge, Tennessee

## Your Day to Day as an EH&S Manager:

• Develops and executes the site’s strategic Environmental, Health & Safety (EH&S) roadmap aligned with corporate objectives, ensuring long‑term planning supports operational and regulatory expectations.

• Fosters a world‑class safety culture through leadership engagement, employee ownership, accountability, hazard reporting, and continuous learning, while conducting field observations, safety walks, and GEMBA activities.

• Serves as the principal advisor to operations leadership on environmental compliance, occupational health, industrial safety, regulatory requirements, and risk management across all functional areas.

• Integrates EH&S into operational planning, manufacturing readiness, engineering changes, commissioning activities, new program execution, and equipment or facility design reviews to ensure hazard controls and safe work practices.

• Builds strong cross‑functional partnerships with Operations, Engineering, Licensing, Quality, Security, Maintenance, Human Resources, and Program Management to proactively identify, evaluate, and mitigate operational risk.

• Drives continuous improvement through leading indicators, trend analysis, root cause methodologies, and performance metrics, recommending operational improvements and capital investments that enhance compliance, sustainability, and worker safety.

• Ensures organizational readiness for internal audits, customer assessments, and regulatory inspections; coordinate these activities and maintains regulatory documentation supporting compliance and operational readiness.

• Establishes, implements, and maintains EH&S standards, policies, procedures, operating expectations, and hazard control programs, exercising stop‑work authority when unsafe or non‑compliant conditions arise.

• Leads investigations involving significant safety, environmental, operational events, injuries, near misses, process deviations, or high‑potential incidents, ensuring structured root cause analysis and sustainable corrective actions.

• Monitors corrective action effectiveness, verify timely closure of findings, and share organizational lessons learned to prevent recurrence, supporting the Corrective Action Program (CAP).

• Leads environmental compliance programs ensuring adherence to EPA, state, local, federal, and corporate environmental requirements, overseeing air emissions, waste management, stormwater, wastewater, chemical management, pollution prevention, and environmental monitoring.

• Ensures environmental permits, reports, inspections, and regulatory submissions are accurate and on schedule, while developing long‑term environmental sustainability and compliance improvement strategies.

• Leads comprehensive occupational safety programs across manufacturing, maintenance, laboratories, testing, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness, ensuring compliance with OSHA and applicable consensus standards.

• Oversees industrial hygiene programs covering exposure monitoring, respiratory protection, hearing conservation, ergonomics, asbestos, lead, and hazardous material controls, ensuring proper evaluation of new equipment or processes for adequate hazard controls.

• Leads hazard identification activities including job hazard analyses, process hazard reviews, risk assessments, and operational safety evaluations, supporting engineered and administrative controls and safe work practices.

• Partner with Engineering and Operations to integrate safety into equipment design, manufacturing processes, and facility modifications, supporting readiness reviews, startup activities, and Operational Readiness Reviews (ORRs).

• Champions Human Performance Improvement (HPI), behavior‑based safety, operational discipline, and leadership accountability programs, coaching supervisors and managers to model effective safety leadership.

• Maintains comprehensive knowledge of OSHA, EPA, NFPA, ANSI, Tennessee environmental regulations, and corporate policies, coordinating regulatory inspections, customer audits, internal compliance assessments, and follow‑up corrective action plans.

• Supports emergency preparedness, emergency response teams, fire protection, spill response, evacuation planning, crisis management exercises, and business continuity activities, coordinating drills and emergency training.

• Develops and maintains comprehensive EH&S performance metrics including: Total Recordable Incident Rate (TRIR), Days Away, Restricted or Transferred (DART), lost time incident rate, near-miss reporting, leading safety indicators, Corrective Action Program (CAP) performance, environmental compliance metrics, audit performance, training completion, industrial hygiene exposure trends, regulatory findings, safety observation participation.

• Prepares executive-level reports and dashboards communicating organizational performance, emerging risks, and improvement opportunities.

## Required Qualifications:

• Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Occupational Safety, Industrial Hygiene, Engineering, Environmental Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

• Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible EH&S leadership experience within highly regulated industrial or manufacturing environments.

• Demonstrated experience leading environmental compliance and occupational safety programs supporting complex manufacturing operations.

• Strong working knowledge of OSHA, EPA, NFPA, ANSI, and DOE/NNSA regulatory frameworks.

• Experience conducting incident investigations utilizing formal root cause methodologies.

• Demonstrated success implementing safety culture improvement initiatives.

• Strong leadership, communication, facilitation, and influencing skills.

• Must be a U.S. citizen.

• Must be able to obtain and maintain a U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) clearance.

## Preferred Qualifications:

• Certified Safety Professional (CSP)

• Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH)

• Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM)

• Certified Energy Manager (CEM)

• Experience supporting DOE, NNSA, NRC, nuclear fuel cycle, uranium enrichment, aerospace, defense, chemical processing, or other high-consequence operations.

• Experience supporting startup, commissioning, or operational readiness of new manufacturing facilities.

• Experience implementing Human Performance Improvement (HPI) principles.

• Familiarity with ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 management systems.

• Experience with digital EH&S management systems, corrective action databases, environmental monitoring platforms, and data analytics tools.

With more than 7,800 employees, BWXT has 14 major operating sites in the U.S., Canada and the U.K. We are the sole manufacturer of naval nuclear reactors for U.S. submarines and aircraft carriers. Our company supplies precision manufactured components, services and fuel for the commercial nuclear power industry across four continents. Our joint ventures provide environmental restoration and operations management at a dozen U.S. Department of Energy and NASA facilities. BWXT’s technology is driving advances in medical radioisotope production in North America and microreactors for various defense and space applications. For more information, visit www.bwxt.com. Follow us on LinkedIn, X, Facebook and Instagram.

Welcome to BWXT
We believe in empowering our employees and cultivating a dynamic workplace that fosters growth and collaboration. Whether you’re an experienced professional or just starting your career, you'll find opportunities to challenge yourself, learn from seasoned experts, and contribute to nuclear innovation. We require a diverse range of skills to support our work in the markets that drive our business and welcome candidates from all backgrounds and life stages who are passionate about making a difference.

BWXT is People Strong, Innovation Driven - be part of BWXT’s innovation hub. BWXT’s Lynchburg Technology Center (LTC) consists of five discrete laboratory operations, namely, Nuclear Materials Engineering (NME), Radioisotope & Analytical Chemistry Laboratory (RACL), Nondestructive Evaluation & Inspection Systems (NDE&IS), Metallurgical Laboratory (MET), and Advanced Fuel Development (ADVF). This organization operates under an NRC license with radioactive facilities dealing with special nuclear material as well as by-product materials.

The Non-Destructive Evaluation and Inspection Systems (NDE&IS) group at LTC research, develops, and builds custom non-destructive inspection systems for both internal and external customers. These non-destructive evaluation (NDE) systems are mostly based on ultrasonic testing but can involve electromagnetic (i.e., eddy current and magnetic) testing or vision systems. NDE&IS also supports the development of advanced induction heating applications.

The NDE&IS group is comprised of ten staff members that provide physics, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, software engineering, and system build up capabilities. NDE&IS maintains extensive capabilities for modeling ultrasonic wave propagation, ultrasonic inspections, and eddy current inspections. NDE&IS also has enterprise level finite element modeling (FEM) capability for electromagnetics, thermal, and stress analysis. To further support the buildup of these systems NDE&IS has full electrical, electronics, and printed circuit board development capabilities. NDE&IS also has in-house machining capabilities to support rapid buildup of mechanical devices.

If you are looking for a career where your experience is valued, innovative thinking is fostered, and barrier-free teamwork is embraced every day, then this opportunity is for you.

## Position Overview:

As a Non‑Destructive Evaluation Development Engineer, you will work alongside a team of engineers and technicians to support the research, design, and development of advanced NDE systems. In this role, you will assess customer needs, develop innovative custom system concepts, collaborate with clients on cost proposals, and lead the creation of specialized non‑destructive inspection tests.

## Location:

The position will be based on site in Lynchburg, VA at LTC.

## Your Day to Day as a Non-Destructive Evaluation Development Engineer:

• Assess candidate non-destructive evaluation needs and develop design concepts for custom system development to meet those needs.

• Work with potential customers to prepare and submit cost proposals for the development of custom systems.

• Design and develop non-destructive inspection tests.

• Perform NDE system design including specifying subsystem components such as scanners, NDE instruments, and data acquisition instruments.

• Conduct system verification testing of an inspection method or system.

• Implement modifications to the inspection or testing system as needed to obtain the correct results.

## Required Qualifications:

• A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in physics or engineering is required.

• A minimum of four (4) years of NDE system or inspection development related experience with emphasis on ultrasonic testing is required.

• Must be a self-starter, capable of working as part of a team, and occasionally independently.

• Must have excellent oral, written, and interpersonal skills.

• Must be a U.S. citizen.

• Must be able to obtain and maintain a U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) or Department of Defense (DOD) security clearance as required.

## Preferred Qualifications:

• Experience in numerical modeling for simulating ultrasonic inspections.

• Experience in robotics and automation to support the development of automated ultrasonic inspection systems.

• Possession of an NDE Level III certification.

## What We Offer:

• Competitive salary and benefits package, including health, dental, and retirement plans.

• Flexible work schedules and paid time off to promote a healthy work-life balance.

• Professional development opportunities, including mentorship programs and sponsorship for continuing education.

• An inclusive atmosphere that celebrates new perspectives and supports collaboration between different generations.

• The chance to be part of a mission-driven organization making a positive impact on the future of energy.

• Opportunities for continuous learning and training to grow throughout your career!

• Implement Lean Manufacturing, TPS, and Six Sigma methodologies to eliminate waste, optimize material flow, increase inventory accuracy, and improve warehouse productivity and delivery performance.
• Support implementation and continuous improvement of ERP, MRP, WMS, TMS, MES, barcode/RFID, real‑time location, and automated inventory‑tracking systems; utilize data analytics for decision‑making and performance enhancement.

• MBA or Master’s degree in a relevant field.

## Huawei Canada has an immediate 8-12 month Co-op opening for an Engineer.

## About the team:

Huawei Canada's Advanced Optical Technology Lab focuses on advanced R&D in high-performance optical communications and networking. Our expert team specializes in transmission algorithms, systems, physics, and AI-driven optical network management. The lab engages in projects ranging from deep research to developing key product features, actively participating in standards organizations and collaborative research with partners. Our multicultural environment fosters innovation, mentorship, and a passion for learning. If you thrive on solving complex technical challenges, this lab is your ideal place.

## About the job:

• Working on the next generation of short-reach and data center interconnect (DCI) networks. In this role you will focus on the design and simulation of Intensity-Modulated Direct-Detection (IMDD) transmission systems operating over cutting-edge Hollow-Core Fiber (HCF). Given the physical properties of HCF, efficient signaling and equalization methods are fundamental to achieve cost and power efficient optical links.

• Modeling of end-to-end non-coherent optical transmission system.

• Modeling of Hollow-Core Fiber and the impact of gas absorption on the transmission.

• Exploring efficient signaling and equalization to combat channel induced fading profiles.

• Studying the impact of high launch power on the system reach and performance.

The total target annual compensation (based on 2,080 hours per year) ranges from $58,000 to $104,000 depending on education, experience, and demonstrated expertise.

In addition, you will:

• Provide strategic and operational leadership for the Bank’s facilities services, workplace operations and property portfolio, ensuring safe, efficient and reliable service delivery across owned and leased spaces.

• Oversee facilities operations, maintenance programs, vendor performance and service delivery models to support a high-quality workplace experience and the effective operation of critical environments.

• Lead medium- and long-term planning for facilities services, including operational priorities, lifecycle management, workplace strategies, policies and investment planning.

• Manage budgets, work plans, performance measures and service levels, ensuring effective stewardship of resources and alignment with corporate priorities.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with internal stakeholders, service providers and external partners to deliver facilities services that meet evolving business needs.

What you need to succeed
You are a strategic thinker and an experienced leader who can balance long-term planning with operational excellence.

You have:

• Significant leadership experience in facilities management, workplace services, property management, engineering, building operations, real estate, or a related field.

• Experience leading large and complex operational portfolios, including multi-million-dollar operating and capital budgets.

• Strong business acumen and the ability to align facilities investments and services with organizational priorities.

• Demonstrated success leading high-performing teams and developing a culture of engagement, accountability, and collaboration.

• People leadership with a proven ability to build, inspire, and develop high-performing teams while fostering a culture of trust, accountability, inclusion, and continuous improvement.

• Exceptional relationship management and stakeholder engagement skills.

• Experience managing external service providers and complex contractual relationships.

• Experience applying risk management, governance, performance measurement, and continuous improvement practices.

• A client-focused mindset and a commitment to service excellence.

## Nice-to-have

• Experience overseeing critical infrastructure or mission-critical facilities.

• Experience working in a highly regulated or public-sector environment.

Your education and experience
This position requires a bachelor’s degree in engineering, architecture, facilities management, business administration, project management, real estate, or a related discipline and a minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible leadership experience in facilities management, property management, engineering, building operations, infrastructure management, workplace services, or a related field. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.

We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. ## Ottawa, Canada - Hybrid

We are seeking an entry level Engineer (Physical AI) to join the Pathfinding Studio within the Engineering Innovation Office. In this role, you will research and develop next generation physical AI dataflow algorithms, architectures, and virtual system models for humanoid robotics contributing to pathfinding research. You will work across perception, planning, control, and learning to enable intelligent humanoid behaviors, with particular emphasis on hand and arm manipulation.

Responsibilities:

• Research, design, develop, and maintain end-to-end physical AI dataflows for humanoid robotics, connecting simulation, data generation, model training, evaluation, and deployment.

• Develop, deploy and evaluate algorithms and models for humanoid perception, motion planning, manipulation, and learning.

• Build humanoid simulations using MuJoCo, NVIDIA Isaac Sim, or comparable tools, including models of articulated hands, arms, sensors, and environments.

• Create and curate simulation and real-world datasets; define interfaces, schemas, synchronization methods, and quality checks for multimodal robotics data.

• Develop domain-randomization, synthetic-data, imitation-learning, reinforcement-learning, sim-to-real and real-to-sim workflows.

• Analyze model and controller behavior, establish performance metrics, identify failure modes, and document results.

• Collaborate with software, AI, robotics, and hardware teams to translate research concepts into reproducible prototypes and deployable solutions.

• Bachelor’s degree with relevant experience, or an advanced degree, in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

• Strong experience in algorithm design and mathematical modeling for humanoid robots or other highly articulated robotic systems.

• Hands-on experience with MuJoCo, NVIDIA Isaac Sim, or similar physics-based robotics simulation platforms.

• Experience modeling and controlling humanoid hands and arms, including kinematics, dynamics, grasping, manipulation, trajectory generation, and contact rich interaction.

• Experience with data collection/teleop based sim2real and real2sim pipeline and framework.

• Experience developing robotics software and models in Python and/or C/C++ on Linux.

• Ability to design experiments, analyze model and controller performance, and communicate findings through clear technical documentation.

• Experience working with CPU- and GPU-based development environments and version-controlled software workflows.

• Experience with physical humanoid hand and arm manipulation is a plus.

This posting is for a new vacancy. The expected annual pay range for this position is $65,500 - $82,000. This position is also eligible for bonus opportunities. Please note that the final offer amount will be dependent on geographic location, applicable experience, and skillset of the candidate.

Renesas Canada must at all times comply with U.S. and Canadian export control legislative requirements. All positions at Renesas Canada have direct or indirect access to this technology. As a result, it is necessary for Renesas Canada to determine if it would need an export license for new employees. To do so, we ask all candidates for employment whether their most recent country of citizenship or permanent residence is one of the countries specified in the export controls laws or regulations.

Renesas recognizes that you are entitled to human rights and privacy protections in the workplace and takes these obligations seriously. As such, we want you to know that your decision to complete the export control questions is entirely voluntary. Regrettably, should you choose not to complete these questions, we cannot consider you for employment because doing so would jeopardize our ability to comply with the applicable export controls laws. Should you choose to complete the questions, we will use the information collected only to determine if we would need an export license to employ you and not for any other purpose.

Successful candidates must be eligible to meet the requirements of U.S. export control regulations, including (if applicable) the issuance of any required export license prior to starting employment at Renesas Canada. ## About the positions

We are seeking innovative and skilled Developers to join our Retail Payments Supervision team! We are a collaborative and diverse team within ITS with the mission to carry out the roadmap of an effective regulatory IT platform to meet the requirements of the Bank of Canada’s role in supervising payment service providers (PSPs). We are also beginning work on two new mandates: Stable Coin and Consumer-driven Banking.

Lead by the Director of the Retail Payments Supervision portfolio, you will join a dynamic and highly skilled team working together to design, develop, and support our regulatory IT platform built on the Power Platform.

Further, you will have the full support of your leader and teammates to enhance your skills, experiment, and further your career through our customizable Learning & Development programs across various domains (IT, Programming, Architecture, Analytics, etc.) and relevant certifications.

What you will do
As a Developer, you will be responsible for developing new features and maintaining existing components for the Bank’s RPS regulatory IT platform using the Microsoft technology stack, comprised of Power Pages (Portal), Model Driven Apps, Custom PCF controls, SharePoint, Power Automate Flows, Azure services (Function Apps, APIM) and multiple system integrations.

## More specifically, you will:

• Contribute to the development of the Power Platform application and peripheral technologies

• Analyze, design and implement enhancements to meet business requirements

• Maintain collaborative relationships with internal clients and external counterparts

• Perform technical and root-cause analysis on issues and make recommendations for correction

• Create working procedures and documentation on solutions and populate knowledge databases, testing plans and results

• Apply a continuous improvement mindset, by identifying innovative ways of doing or providing services to our clients; changing or reconfiguring approaches to improve efficiency and capacity

• Ensure compliance with audit requirements during the support and maintenance of applications

• Provide second and third-line support, including evening and weekend paid overtime work, as required

What you need to succeed
You have a strong attention to detail with the ability to rank tasks per priority, meet deadlines and perform multiple tasks concurrently. You also can communicate effectively and maintain co-operative working relationships with the other project members and IT teams.

In addition, you have:

• Experience developing within Dynamics 365 and Power Platform or other CRM systems

• Experience building custom APIs and Plug-ins

• Proven experience with C# programming language and .NET Framework

• Proven experience with web portal development in a Microsoft or equivalent environment

• Experience developing and maintaining HTML5, CSS, JavaScript web portal applications

• Experience working with business analysts or user experience (UX) designers to creatively translate business requirements and designs into interactive web portal functionality

• Experience and understanding of source control systems, including advanced branching and merging techniques

## Nice-to-have

• Experience with Liquid or equivalent templating engine

• Experience in writing programming scripts using PowerShell

Your education and experience
Your combined education and work experience demonstrate that you have the proficiencies and skills for the role. We are ideally seeking candidates with a relevant degree/diploma and 3+ years of relevant experience for the job grade 15 role and 5+ years of experience for the job grade 16 role.

## Innovative Mindset

We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. We seek individuals who can think critically about data, question existing processes, and find ways to simplify our work while embracing change and new ways of doing things.

Language requirement
The Bank’s work environment is conducive to the use of both of Canada’s official languages - English and French. Although the position language requirement is English or French essential, we do encourage everyone to improve their second language proficiency for future career growth and to contribute towards fostering a bilingual environment.

## What you need to know

• • Priority will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents

• Security level required: Be eligible to obtain Secret

• There will be no relocation assistance provided

• Please save a copy of the job poster. Once the closing date has passed, it will no longer be available.

• The official title for this position is “Developer ”

## Hybrid Work Model

The Bank offers work arrangements that provide employees with flexibility, enable high-performing teams, and support an excellent workplace culture. Most employees can telework from home for a portion of each month as part of the Bank’s hybrid work model, and they are expected on site at the Bank location a minimum of 12 days per month to help build connections between colleagues. You must live in Canada, and within reasonable commuting distance of the office.

What you can expect from us
This is a great opportunity to join a leading organization and be part of a high-performing team. We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to meet your needs at every stage of your life and career. For more information on key benefits please visit A great deal to consider.

## About the team:

The Web Technology Lab focuses on two areas of next-generation web technology: Web Rendering and Web Agents. Web Rendering explores the Chromium rendering architecture, including the development of concurrent web layout systems and the use of vertical integration opportunities to optimize performance and user experience. Web Agents explores how AI agents understand websites, leverage web capabilities, and complete tasks for users. This includes browser-native agents and emerging technologies such as WebMCP, helping evolve the web from a space primarily designed for people to browse and interact with into one where people and AI agents can work together. Together, these efforts aim to make the web more efficient to render and easier for both people and AI agents to use.

## About the job:

• Research how state-of-the-art web agents (browser-use, computer-use, MCP-based agents) interact with real-world websites — identifying failure modes, reliability gaps, and capability ceilings.

• Study how different web tech stacks affect agent performance, and define design patterns that make sites more agent-friendly.

• Investigate how LLMs perceive and reason about web content (HTML, rendered DOM, screenshots, accessibility trees) and which representations are most effective for different tasks.

• Prototype new architectures, interaction models, and agent frameworks to empirically test hypotheses and bridge Web capabilities with AI-driven Agents.

The total target annual compensation (based on 2,080 hours per year) ranges from $106,000 to $156,000 depending on education, experience, and demonstrated expertise.

Le technicien en contrôle des satellites (TCS) relève du Superviseur des opérations satellites (SSO) et joue un rôle essentiel dans l’exploitation et la maintenance des systèmes satellitaires. Ce poste implique l’exploitation des systèmes de télémesure, poursuite et télécommande en temps réel, la surveillance de l’état des satellites, l’envoi de commandes ainsi que le soutien à l’identification et à la résolution des anomalies.

CareersInnerInfo
Responsabilités

• Effectuer les opérations planifiées en temps réel des satellites et des systèmes TT&C conformément aux procédures approuvées

• Exécuter les passes satellites incluant les commandes, la vérification de la télémesure et le téléchargement des données

• Effectuer les activités après passage (transfert de fichiers, déconfiguration des équipements, consignation des événements)

• Initier des actions correctives en cas de problèmes procéduraux

• Examiner les produits opérationnels (quotidiens, hebdomadaires et replanifiés)

• S’assurer que les instructions spéciales sont correctement intégrées aux opérations

• Soutenir et diriger les activités de récupération d’anomalies lorsque requis

• Effectuer la maintenance quotidienne des postes de travail

• Produire des rapports de perte de données conformément aux procédures

• Fournir un soutien opérationnel aux équipes internes et aux intervenants externes autorisés

• Maintenir les protocoles de sécurité et signaler tout accès non autorisé

• Effectuer toute autre tâche connexe dans le cadre du posteQualifications

• Excellente maîtrise du français et de l’anglais, à l’oral et à l’écrit

The Satellite Control Technician (SCT) is responsible to the Supervisor, Satellite Operations (SSO) and plays a critical role in the operation and maintenance of satellite systems. • Strong attention to detail and high level of accuracy

• Ability to work under pressure in a fast-paced environment

• Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills

• Ability to work independently and as part of a team

• Strong communication and interpersonal skills

## Position Overview

We are looking for a Quality Assurance and Compliance Specialist to ensure products, assemblies, processes, and quality systems meet customer, contractual, regulatory, and internal quality requirements. This role supports manufacturing and production operations through inspection planning, product verification, nonconformance management, root cause investigations, corrective actions, and continuous improvement initiatives.In addition to product quality activities, the Quality Assurance and Compliance Specialist supports the organization's quality management system, compliance programs, process development initiatives, audit activities, and future accreditation efforts. The role works cross-functionally to promote quality excellence, maintain regulatory and customer compliance, and contribute to ongoing improvements in products, processes, and quality systems.

CareersInnerInfo

## Responsibilities

• • Develop and maintain inspection plans based on product requirements and risk.

• Perform in-process and final inspections of products and assemblies.

• Inspect electronic assemblies, printed circuit boards, and wire harnesses for conformance to specifications.

• Interpret drawings, schematics, bills of materials, and test reports to verify compliance.

• Document, track, and help manage nonconformances in accordance with established processes.

• Support root cause analysis and corrective action activities related to product and process issues.

• Analyze inspection results and trends to identify quality risks and improvement opportunities.

• Collaborate with Production, Engineering, Project Management, and Quality teams to resolve quality concerns.

• Provide guidance and training to production personnel and junior inspectors as needed.

• Support internal, customer, regulatory, and accreditation audits.

• Develop, maintain, and improve quality procedures, work instructions, records, and related documentation.

• Assist with quality management system activities, compliance initiatives, and maintenance of quality records.

• Support process development, implementation, standardization, and continuous improvement initiatives across manufacturing and quality functions.

• Participate in corrective action investigations, process improvement initiatives, and effectiveness reviews.

• Contribute to future accreditation activities and ongoing quality program development.

• Apply critical thinking to identify discrepancies, assess impact on quality, evaluate inspection results, and support development of effective solutions.

• Document escapes or deviations, participate in investigations, and contribute to corrective actions independently and within cross-functional teams.

• Perform other duties as required within the scope of the role.

## Qualifications

• • Diploma in Electronics Engineering Technology, Manufacturing Technology, Quality Assurance, or a related technical discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.

• Minimum of 5 years of experience in quality assurance, quality control, manufacturing, engineering, process improvement, or a related technical discipline.

• Experience in aerospace, defense, medical device, or other regulated industries is an asset.

• Strong knowledge of electronics manufacturing processes including PCB assembly, cable and wire harness fabrication, and electro-mechanical assemblies.

• Proficiency inspecting to IPC-A-610 and IPC/WHMA-A-620 standards.

• Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics, engineering drawings, specifications, bills of materials, and test reports.

• Experience supporting quality management systems such as ISO 9001, AS9100, or other regulated industry standards, such as NADCAP.

• Experience with nonconformance reporting processes and systems.

• Practical experience with root cause analysis methodologies such as 5 Whys, Fishbone, and corrective action processes.

• Experience supporting audits, corrective action programs, and continuous improvement initiatives.

• Experience developing, implementing, or improving processes, procedures, work instructions, or quality documentation.

• Familiarity with inspection tools, measurement equipment, and verification techniques.

• Strong attention to detail with a high level of accuracy and workmanship.

• Ability to analyze data, identify trends, and highlight risks or improvement opportunities.

• Effective communication skills with the ability to document findings and explain technical information clearly.

• Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and collaborate effectively across teams.

• Ability to coach and provide guidance to production personnel and junior inspectors.

## Additional Requirements

• IPC certification in IPC-A-610 and/or IPC/WHMA-A-620 is an asset.

• • Internal auditor training or experience is an asset.

• Experience with continuous improvement methodologies such as Lean, Six Sigma, or equivalent is an asset.

• Experience supporting customer, regulatory, certification, accreditation, or NADCAP audits is an asset.

• Experience supporting quality system implementation, maintenance, or accreditation activities is an asset.

Compensation

• $50,000 to $75,000

Position Type

• Full-time

• We have 1 available position

## Position Overview:

As our High Temp Thermo-Mechanical Properties Test Lead, you will be part of a team assisting multiple nuclear development projects in Lynchburg, VA. The individual will be responsible for defining standard test methodologies, performing materials testing, and mentoring peers; while supporting a wide variety of programs for space, defense, and commercial customers.

## Location:

On-site in Lynchburg, VA at the Advanced Technologies Office

## Your Day to Day as a High Thermo-Mechanical Properties Test Lead:

• Develop and implement material characterization methodologies and testing capabilities focused on thermo-physical properties, including temperature-dependent diffusivity, heat capacity, coefficient of thermal expansion, and mechanical strength.

• Operate and maintain a high temperature mechanical testing furnace along with a suite of characterization instruments such as Laser Flash Analysis (LFA), Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC), Simultaneous Thermal Analysis (STA), and Dilatometry to evaluate novel nuclear fuel forms.

• Perform thermo-physical property characterization on samples from diverse R&D and prototype production programs.

• Collaborate closely with materials scientists, chemical engineers, and other stakeholders to identify and apply appropriate characterization techniques that provide critical data to support R&D objectives.

• Mentor and support the broader team in the characterization of ceramics, metals, composites, and nuclear fuel materials.

• Support the operations manager in the build-out, commissioning, and safety documentation for the testing facility.

## Required Qualifications:

• A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in engineering (e.g. Materials Science and Engineering, Mechanical Engineer, Nuclear Engineer, Chemical Engineer) or Physics is required.

• A minimum of seven (7) years of relevant experience is required.

• Must have strong organizational and communication skills with the ability to multi-task.

• Must be a U.S. Citizen.

• Must be able to obtain and maintain a U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) or Department of Defense (DOD) security clearance, whichever is required.

## Preferred Qualifications:

• MS or PhD in materials science, chemistry, or a related field is highly desired.

• Strong background in characterization of inorganic materials, including nuclear materials, metals, ceramics, and composites.

• Experience with ASTM standards for thermo-physical property testing.

• Familiarity with ISO or NQA-1 quality programs for materials testing.

• Hands-on experience or foundational knowledge in thermal diffusivity (LFA), calorimetry (DSC/STA), dilatometry, and mechanical testing at elevated temperatures exceeding 1200 °C (2240 °F).

## What We Offer:

• Flexible work schedules and paid time off to promote a healthy work-life balance.

• Professional development opportunities, including mentorship programs and sponsorship for continuing education.

• An inclusive atmosphere that celebrates new perspectives and supports collaboration between different generations.

March Networks is an established global leader in the video surveillance industry and works with the world’s largest retailers and banking institutions. Our goal is to create a positive working environment where all of our employees can thrive. When you join our team, you’ll enjoy flexibility and support for a healthy work-life balance, as well as the professional development opportunities needed to advance your career. At March Networks, we value your hard work, creativity and your passionate desire to deliver only the best to our customers, partners and each other.

## Role overview

This role leads end‑to‑end Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) and Integrated Business Planning (IBP) for March Networks and Vivotek hardware (SSS LOB). The Senior Manager is accountable for aligning demand, supply, and financial plans, and for translating those plans into executable build, capacity, and inventory commitments with our global Contract Manufacturing partners, including Delta and Sanmina. The role works in close partnership with the Senior Professional, Procurement, who owns supplier strategy and commercial negotiations.

## Key responsibilities

## S&OP / IBP ownership

• Architect, implement, and continuously improve the S&OP / IBP framework, calendar, and governance across Sales, Operations, Finance, Product, and Engineering.

• Define the S&OP key metrics, including standard templates, KPIs, and RACI, to ensure a disciplined, repeatable process.

• Lead monthly demand, supply, and executive S&OP reviews; ensure decisions are translated into MPS/MRP, capacity plans, and commercial commitments.

• Integrate demand forecasts, supply plans, and financial plans to deliver revenue, service level, and inventory objectives while managing risk for both March Networks and Vivotek demand (SSS LOB).

• Benchmark and embed best practices, tools, and analytics to support scenario planning and decision quality.

## Demand, supply, and inventory planning

• Lead development of a consensus demand plan by integrating sales input from March Networks and Vivotek sales regions, market intelligence, and statistical forecasts, including NPI demand.

• Oversee forecasting methodologies, forecast accuracy and metrics, and demand risk/opportunity management.

• Work with Operations / Supply Chain to translate demand into capacity, supply, and inventory plans that meet service and working capital targets.

• Lead scenario planning for upside/downside demand, component constraints, customer priorities, inventory investment, and revenue recovery strategies.

## Contract manufacturing planning and logistics

• Serve as the planning interface to global contract manufacturing partners, including Delta, Sanmina, and future partners across North America, Europe, and Asia.

• Manage a rolling 6–12-month forecast, including fixed, flex, and forecast windows, with MPS/MRP visibility and clear rules for expedites, reschedules, and minimum order quantities to stabilize planning and ensure supply continuity.

• Manage raw material risk and liability exposure by leveraging Kinaxis to provide visibility into work orders, WIP, purchase orders, and inventory, reconciled against demand.

• Support global third-party and outsourced logistics locations for inventory management, configuration capabilities, and direct order fulfillment, including inbound, outbound, and intercompany shipment logistics.

## BOM and material availability

• Use Bill of Materials (BOM) analysis to inform S&OP decisions, including long lead‑time risk and early‑purchase strategies, in partnership with Procurement.

• Serve as the point of escalation for material shortages impacting builds, pilot runs, and volume product builds, coordinating mitigation across planning, engineering, procurement, and suppliers.

• Incorporate supply risks identified by Procurement (EOL, allocation, tariff, single-source) into supply plans and scenario reviews.

## Executive engagement and change leadership

• Present S&OP outcomes, supply risks, and scenario analyses to executive leadership, driving data‑driven decisions.

• Champion cross‑functional alignment between Sales, Product, Engineering, Operations, Finance, and Procurement, resolving conflicts and enforcing accountability for planning inputs and actions.

• Lead change management to elevate S&OP maturity, including process improvements, tool adoption, and capability building across the organization.

• Participate in Product Line readiness and gate reviews, clearly articulating supply status, risks, and mitigation plans.

## Performance management and governance

• Define and monitor planning KPIs, including forecast accuracy and bias, OTIF, inventory turns, capacity utilization, material availability, and NPI launch readiness.

• Ensure that S&OP decisions are reflected in ERP/APS data and material masters.

• Drive continuous improvement in planning, quantifying financial and operational benefits (e.g., reduced expedites, improved fill rates, lower obsolescence).

## Qualifications and experience

• 8+ years of experience in supply chain, operations, or planning in the high‑tech / networking or electronics industry.

• 5+ years of direct experience leading S&OP/IBP or integrated demand/supply planning processes, ideally in a hardware or systems environment.

• Experience working with contract manufacturers and outsourced logistics providers, including forecast commitments and liability management.

• Strong understanding of MRP/MPS, capacity planning, and inventory management, and how they connect to S&OP and financial planning.

• Proficiency with ERP and planning systems (e.g., SAP, Kinaxis, or similar) and advanced Excel/analytics.

• Excellent communication, facilitation, and leadership skills; proven ability to influence cross‑functional stakeholders and executives and to drive decisions under time pressure.

• Strong analytical and problem‑solving skills, including financial analysis and scenario modeling.

• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Business, or related field; APICS/ASCM certification (CPIM, CSCP) or a Master’s degree is an asset.

## Personal attributes

• Strategic, systems thinker who can connect commercial and operational decisions end‑to‑end.

• Highly collaborative and team‑oriented, with the presence to lead cross‑functional forums and executive reviews.

• Comfortable operating in a fast‑paced, ambiguous environment with multiple concurrent NPI programs and evolving customer demand.

• Results‑driven with a focus on disciplined execution, continuous improvement, and measurable impact on revenue and service.

Why Work at March Networks?

· Global Exposure

· Medical/Dental benefits offered immediately from Day 1

· Health club reimbursement

· Professional development support

· Company holiday closure

March Networks is an equal opportunity employer and supports a diverse workforce.

Accommodations are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process. Applicants can make their accommodation needs known to us in their application.

Please note March Networks uses AI as part of the recruitment process.

## Role overview

This role provides advanced strategic procurement for March Networks and Vivotek hardware (SSS LOB). The Senior Procurement Specialist builds and manages a world‑class supply base, leads supplier and contract manufacturer commercial negotiations, and manages component risk and lifecycle to enable successful product hardware build strategies with our global Contract Manufacturing partners, including Delta and Sanmina. The role works in close partnership with the Senior Manager, S&OP, who owns demand, supply, and inventory planning.

## Key responsibilities

## Strategic procurement for SSS LOB

• Provide advanced procurement support to the Hardware Engineering organization throughout the product development lifecycle, from concept through volume production, for the Taipei, Poland, Milan, and Ottawa design teams.

• Develop and maintain strategic supplier relationships across key hardware commodities, including Memory/SOC/ICs/processors, PCBs, connectors, fans, and electro‑mechanical components.

• Lead supply risk management, including geopolitical, sanctions, tariff, lifecycle, allocation, and single-source component risks, while developing mitigation strategies.

• Act as the primary business interface between supply partners, Hardware Engineering, Product Line Management, and Operations.

• Lead component price negotiations and manage commercial release milestones to meet build schedules, cost, and margin objectives.

• Evaluate supplier capability, reliability, capacity, financial health, and cost competitiveness to support both NPI and long‑term supply strategies.

## Contract manufacturing and outsourcing

• Support global contract manufacturing partners, including Delta, Sanmina, and future partners across North America, Europe, and Asia, on commercial and sourcing matters.

• Drive and negotiate cost models with existing and new outsource partners to maximize the SSS LOB’s margin contribution.

• In collaboration with the Technical Operations team, engage contract manufacturers early and formally in DFM/DFA by conducting joint design reviews, BOM rationalization, and component risk assessments to ensure manufacturability, test strategy, and lifecycle/obsolescence considerations are built in.

## BOM analysis, risk, and lifecycle management

• Drive component portfolio rationalization across all four design teams to reduce the number of suppliers and components being supported.

• Perform in‑depth Bill of Materials (BOM) analysis to inform procurement and S&OP decisions, including long lead‑time risk and early‑purchase recommendations.

• Drive end‑of‑life (EOL) component analysis, Product Change Notification (PCN) reviews, and dual‑sourcing strategies to protect continuity of supply.

• Assess manufacturing cost structures for NPI designs and provide component‑level and finished‑goods cost models to Product Line Management and Finance.

• Support the S&OP team in resolving material shortages impacting builds, pilot runs, and volume product builds by working directly with suppliers on recovery.

## Commercial and contractual leadership

• Lead procurement contract, NDA, and commercial term negotiations with key suppliers in alignment with corporate policies and risk appetite.

• Conduct business and financial reviews of potential and existing suppliers to support sourcing decisions and S&OP risk reviews.

• Manage pricing updates and verification for Engineering, Product Line Management, and Finance to ensure alignment of standard costs with S&OP assumptions and financial plans.

## Stakeholder engagement

• Present procurement strategies, supply risks, and savings opportunities to leadership and in S&OP reviews.

• Participate in Product Line readiness and gate reviews, clearly articulating sourcing status, risks, mitigation plans, and commercial implications.

• Contribute to elevating strategic sourcing maturity, including process improvements and tool adoption.

## Performance management and governance

• Monitor procurement KPIs, including material cost variance, savings, supplier on-time delivery, and supplier and component consolidation.

• Ensure that sourcing strategies and pricing are accurately reflected in ERP data, material masters, and procurement records.

• Drive continuous improvement in sourcing and NPI commercialization, quantifying financial benefits (e.g., cost reductions, lower obsolescence, better margins).

## Qualifications and experience

• 7+ years of experience in strategic sourcing, commodity management, or procurement in the high‑tech / networking or electronics industry.

• Hands‑on experience with NPI processes and BOM analysis, including cost modeling, lifecycle/risk assessment, and supplier selection.

• Demonstrated success negotiating complex commercial agreements, including pricing, contracts, and NDAs with semiconductor and electronics suppliers and contract manufacturers.

• Working knowledge of MRP/MPS and how procurement decisions connect to S&OP and financial planning.

• Proficiency with ERP systems (e.g., SAP or similar), sourcing tools, and advanced Excel/analytics; experience with product lifecycle or Agile/PLM systems is an asset.

• Excellent communication and negotiation skills; proven ability to influence cross‑functional stakeholders and suppliers.

• Strong analytical and problem‑solving skills, including cost analysis and supply risk mitigation.

• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Business, or related field; a procurement designation (e.g., CSCMP, CPSM, SCMP) is an asset.

## Personal attributes

• Strategic thinker who can connect commercial, technical, and operational decisions end‑to‑end.

• Highly collaborative, with the credibility to work closely with engineering teams and senior supplier contacts.

• Comfortable operating in a fast‑paced, ambiguous environment with multiple concurrent NPI programs.

## Lead the Technology. Own the Customer. Solve the Hard Problems.
